sentences.zh: 【齊紀八】　屠維單閼，一年。

translations.literal: [Qi Records 8] Xin-you year, one year.
translations.idiomatic: [Qi Records 8] The eighth annal of Qi covers the xinyou year, a single year of the chronicle.

sentences.zh: 東昏侯上永元元年（

translations.literal: First year of Yongyuan, upper reign of Marquis of Eastern Depravity (
translations.idiomatic: The first year of Yongyuan under Marquis Donghun, Part One (

sentences.zh: 己卯，公元四九九年）

translations.literal: jimao, corresponding to the year 499 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jimao, equivalent to 499 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊寅朔，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the new moon day wuyin, a great amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month (wuyin), the court declared a general amnesty and adopted a new reign title.

sentences.zh: 太尉陳顯達督平北將軍崔慧景等軍四萬擊魏，欲復雍州諸郡；

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Chen Xianda supervised the army of forty thousand under General Who Pacifies the North Cui Jingjing and others to attack Wei, intending to recover the various commanderies of Yong Province;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Chen Xianda took command of a forty-thousand-man force led by General Who Pacifies the North Cui Jingjing and others to strike Wei, aiming to retake the commanderies of Yong Province;

sentences.zh: 癸未，魏遣前將軍元英拒之。

translations.literal: On guimou, Wei sent the former general Yuan Ying to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: On guimou, Wei dispatched the former general Yuan Ying to oppose them.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，魏主發鄴。

translations.literal: On yiyou, the Emperor of Wei set out from Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, the Wei emperor departed from Ye.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，帝祀南郊。

translations.literal: On xinmao, the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, the Qi emperor performed the southern suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，魏主至洛陽，過李沖家。

translations.literal: On wuxu, the Emperor of Wei arrived at Luoyang and passed by Li Chong's house.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, the Wei emperor reached Luoyang and went by Li Chong's residence.

sentences.zh: 時臥疾，望之而泣；

translations.literal: At the time Li lay ill in bed; upon seeing him the emperor wept;
translations.idiomatic: Li was then bedridden with illness; the emperor looked upon him and wept;

sentences.zh: 見留守官，語及沖，輒流涕。

translations.literal: whenever he met officials who had remained to guard the capital and the talk turned to Li Chong, he would shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: whenever he met the officials left behind in the capital and the conversation touched on Li Chong, tears would stream down his face.

sentences.zh: 魏主謂任城王澄曰：「朕離京以來，舊俗少變不？」

translations.literal: The Emperor of Wei said to Prince Cheng of Ren: "Since I left the capital, have the old customs changed much or little?"
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor said to Prince Cheng of Ren, "Since I left the capital, have the old ways changed much at all?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「聖化日新。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your sagely transformation renews itself day by day."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Your holy influence grows fresher every day."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕入城，見車上婦人猶戴帽、著小襖，何謂日新！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Since I entered the city I have seen women in carriages still wearing hats and short jackets—what do you mean by 'renewing day by day'!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When I entered the city I still saw women in carts wearing hats and short jackets—what do you mean by 'renewing every day'!"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「著者少，不著者多。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Those who wear them are few; those who do not wear them are many."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Those who still dress that way are few; those who do not are many."

sentences.zh: 帝曰；

translations.literal: The emperor said;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said,

sentences.zh: 「任城，此何言也！

translations.literal: "Prince Ren, what sort of talk is this!
translations.idiomatic: "Prince of Ren, what kind of answer is that!

sentences.zh: 必欲使滿城盡著邪！」

translations.literal: Must you insist that the whole city dress that way!"
translations.idiomatic: Must every person in the whole city dress that way before you will call it changed!"

sentences.zh: 澄與留守官皆免冠謝。

translations.literal: Cheng and the officials who had remained behind all removed their caps and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng and the capital officials who had stayed behind all removed their caps and begged forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，魏大赦。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Wei declared a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 魏主之幸鄴也，李彪迎拜於鄴南，且謝罪。

translations.literal: When the Emperor of Wei had toured Ye, Li Biao met him to bow in welcome south of Ye and also begged forgiveness for his offenses.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei emperor visited Ye, Li Biao went out to welcome him south of the city, bowed, and pleaded for pardon.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕欲用卿，恩李僕射而止。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I wished to employ you, but stopped for the sake of Vice Minister Li."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I meant to use you, but held back out of regard for Vice Minister Li."

sentences.zh: 慰而遣之。

translations.literal: He consoled him and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: He comforted him and let him go.

sentences.zh: 會御史台令史龍文觀告：「太子恂被收之日，有手書自理，彪不以聞。」

translations.literal: At that time the secretary of the Censorate, Long Wenguang, reported: "On the day when Crown Prince Xun was taken into custody there was a note in his own hand pleading his own case, which Biao did not report to the throne."
translations.idiomatic: Then the Censorate clerk Long Wenguang lodged a charge: "On the day Crown Prince Xun was arrested he wrote a plea in his own hand, and Biao never reported it."

sentences.zh: 尚書表收彪赴洛陽。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Works submitted a memorial requesting that Biao be taken into custody and sent to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Works memorialized that Biao be arrested and brought to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 帝以為彪必不然；

translations.literal: The emperor believed that Biao surely had not done so;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was convinced Biao could not have done such a thing;

sentences.zh: 以牛車散載詣洛陽，會赦，得免。

translations.literal: he had him carried to Luoyang in open ox-carts, and when the amnesty came he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: he had him conveyed to Luoyang in ordinary ox-carts without bonds, and when the amnesty was proclaimed he was spared.

sentences.zh: 魏太保齊郡靈王簡卒。

translations.literal: The Grand Preceptor of Wei, Prince Jian of Qi Commandery and Spirit, died.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Grand Preceptor, Prince Jian the Spirited of Qi Commandery, died.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛亥，魏以咸陽王禧為太尉。

translations.literal: In the second month, on xinhai, Wei appointed Prince Xi of Xianyang as Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinhai, Wei made Prince Xi of Xianyang Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 魏主連年在外，馮后私於宦官高菩薩。

translations.literal: The Emperor of Wei had been away from the capital for years on end; Empress Feng carried on a private affair with the eunuch Gao Pusa.
translations.idiomatic: With the Wei emperor away from the capital year after year, Empress Feng took the eunuch Gao Pusa as her secret lover.

sentences.zh: 及帝在懸瓠病篤，后益肆意無所憚，中常侍雙蒙等為之心腹。

translations.literal: When the emperor fell gravely ill at Xuanchi, the empress became all the more reckless and unafraid; the chief eunuch Shuang Meng and others became her trusted inner circle.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor grew critically ill at Xuanchi, the empress grew ever bolder and fearless, and the chief eunuchs Shuang Meng and others became her intimate confidants.

sentences.zh: 彭城公主為宋王劉昶之婦，寡居。

translations.literal: Princess Pengcheng was the wife of Prince Song Liu Chang; she lived as a widow.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Pengcheng had been the wife of Prince Song Liu Chang and now lived in widowhood.

sentences.zh: 后為其母弟北平公馮夙求婚，帝許之；

translations.literal: The empress wished to marry her to her younger brother by the same mother, Duke of Beiping Feng Su, and the emperor consented;
translations.idiomatic: The empress sought a match for her with her uterine younger brother, Duke of Beiping Feng Su, and the emperor agreed;

sentences.zh: 公主不願，後強之。

translations.literal: the princess was unwilling, but the empress forced the matter.
translations.idiomatic: the princess refused, but the empress pressed the marriage upon her.

sentences.zh: 公主密與家僮冒雨詣懸瓠，訴於帝，且具道后所為。

translations.literal: The princess secretly went with a household servant through the rain to Xuanchi to appeal to the emperor and fully recounted what the empress had done.
translations.idiomatic: The princess slipped away with a household servant through the rain to Xuanchi, laid her grievance before the emperor, and told him everything the empress had done.

sentences.zh: 帝疑而秘之。

translations.literal: The emperor harbored doubts but kept the matter secret.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was troubled but kept the affair concealed.

sentences.zh: 后聞之，始懼。

translations.literal: When the empress heard of it, she began to fear.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress learned of this, fear seized her for the first time.

sentences.zh: 陰與母常氏使女巫厭禱，曰：「帝疾若不起，一旦得如文明太后輔少主稱制者，當賞報不貲。」

translations.literal: Secretly she and her mother the Lady Chang had shamans perform curse-laying rites, saying: "If the emperor's illness does not lift and he does not recover, but should one day be like Empress Dowager Wenming assisting a young sovereign and ruling in his name, rewards beyond reckoning shall be given."
translations.idiomatic: In secret she and her mother Lady Chang had sorceresses perform malign rites, saying, "If the emperor's illness does not abate and he does not rise again, but should I one day rule as regent like Empress Dowager Wenming did for a young emperor, your reward shall be beyond counting."

sentences.zh: 帝還洛，收高菩薩、雙蒙等，案問，具伏。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to Luoyang, Gao Pusa, Shuang Meng, and others were arrested and interrogated; they all confessed.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned to Luoyang, Gao Pusa, Shuang Meng, and the rest were seized and examined; they confessed everything.

sentences.zh: 帝在含溫室，夜引后入，賜坐東楹，去御榻二丈餘，命菩薩等陳狀。

translations.literal: The emperor was in the Hanwen Chamber; at night he summoned the empress in and granted her a seat on the eastern pillar, more than two zhang from the imperial couch, and ordered Pusa and the rest to state the facts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was in the Hanwen Chamber. That night he had the empress brought in and gave her a seat by the eastern pillar, more than two zhang from his couch, then ordered Pusa and the others to lay out the whole affair.

sentences.zh: 既而召彭城王勰、北海王詳入坐，曰：「昔為汝嫂，今是路人，但入勿避！」

translations.literal: Then he summoned Prince Xie of Pengcheng and Prince Xiang of Beihai to sit with him and said: "Once she was your sister-in-law; now she is a stranger in the road—yet enter and do not shrink away!"
translations.idiomatic: He then called in Prince Xie of Pengcheng and Prince Xiang of Beihai to sit with him and said, "She was once your sister-in-law; now she is a stranger on the road—yet come in and do not hold back!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「此嫗欲手刃吾脅！

translations.literal: He also said: "This woman wished to cut my flank with her own hand!
translations.idiomatic: He added, "This hag wanted to stab me in the side with her own hand!

sentences.zh: 吾以文明太后家女，不能廢，但虛置宮中，有心庶能自死；

translations.literal: I cannot dismiss her, for she is a daughter of the house of Empress Dowager Wenming; I can only place her idle in the inner palace, hoping in my heart that perhaps she may take her own life;
translations.idiomatic: Because she is a daughter of Empress Dowager Wenming's clan I cannot depose her; I can only keep her idle in the palace, hoping in my heart that she may choose death for herself;

sentences.zh: 汝等勿謂吾猶有情也。」

translations.literal: do not think that I still have feeling for her."
translations.idiomatic: do not imagine that I still harbor affection for her."

sentences.zh: 二王出，賜后辭訣；

translations.literal: The two princes withdrew, and the emperor granted the empress words of farewell;
translations.idiomatic: The two princes withdrew, and the emperor gave the empress her parting words;

sentences.zh: 后再拜，稽首涕泣。

translations.literal: the empress bowed again, touched her forehead to the ground, and wept.
translations.idiomatic: the empress bowed twice, touched her forehead to the ground, and wept.

sentences.zh: 入居後宮。

translations.literal: She entered and dwelt in the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: She went to live in the rear palace.

sentences.zh: 諸嬪御奉之猶如后禮，唯命太子不復朝謁而已。

translations.literal: All the consorts and ladies-in-waiting waited on her still with the rites due an empress; only she was commanded that the crown prince should no longer come to audience.
translations.idiomatic: All the consorts and attendants still served her with empress's rites; the sole command was that the crown prince should no longer attend her.

sentences.zh: 初，馮熙以文明太后之兄尚恭宗女博陵長公主。

translations.literal: Earlier, Feng Xi, as elder brother of Empress Dowager Wenming, married the daughter of Emperor Gongzong, the Long Princess of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Feng Xi, brother of Empress Dowager Wenming, had married Emperor Gongzong's daughter, the Long Princess of Boling.

sentences.zh: 熙有三女，二為皇后，一為左昭儀，由是馮氏貴寵冠群臣，賞賜累巨萬。

translations.literal: Xi had three daughters; two became empresses and one became Senior Lady of Bright Deportment on the left, and thereby the Feng clan's favor and honor topped all ministers, with rewards piling up to tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Xi had three daughters—two became empresses and one Senior Lady of Bright Deportment on the left—so the Feng clan's favor surpassed every other house at court, and their rewards ran into the tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 公主生二子：「誕、修。

translations.literal: The princess bore two sons: Dan and Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: The princess bore two sons, Dan and Xiu.

sentences.zh: 熙為太保，誕為司徒，修為侍中、尚書，庶子聿為黃門郎。

translations.literal: Xi was Grand Preceptor, Dan was Minister of Works, Xiu was Palace Attendant and Minister of the Secretariat, and the son by a concubine, Yu, was Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Xi served as Grand Preceptor, Dan as Minister of Works, Xiu as Palace Attendant and Minister of the Secretariat, and the son by a concubine, Yu, as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎崔光與聿同直，謂聿曰：「君家富貴太盛，終必衰敗。」

translations.literal: Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Cui Guang was on duty together with Yu and said to Yu: "Your family's wealth and honor are too great; in the end they must decline and fall."
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Cui Guang shared a watch with Yu and told him, "Your house is too rich and too grand; in the end it is bound to fall."

sentences.zh: 聿曰：「我家何所負，而君無諒詛我！」

translations.literal: Yu said: "What fault has my family committed, that you curse me without cause!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "What wrong has my family done, that you curse us without cause!"

sentences.zh: 光曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Guang said: "It is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Guang said, "That is not the point.

sentences.zh: 物盛必衰，此天地之常理。

translations.literal: When things reach their height they must decline—this is the constant principle of Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: What flourishes must wither; that is the constant law of Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 若以古事推之，不可不慎。」

translations.literal: If you infer from events of old, you cannot but be cautious."
translations.idiomatic: Judge by what the past records, and you cannot afford to be careless."

sentences.zh: 後歲餘而修敗。

translations.literal: More than a year later Xiu met ruin.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than a year later Xiu was ruined.

sentences.zh: 修性浮競，誕屢戒之，不悛，乃白於太后及帝而杖之。

translations.literal: Xiu's nature was frivolous and contentious; Dan repeatedly warned him, but he would not reform, so Dan reported him to the empress dowager and the emperor and had him beaten with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was flighty and quarrelsome; Dan warned him again and again, but he would not mend his ways, so Dan reported him to the empress dowager and the emperor and had him flogged.

sentences.zh: 修由是恨誕，求藥，使誕左右毒之。

translations.literal: Because of this Xiu hated Dan; he sought poison and had Dan's attendants administer it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu therefore hated Dan, obtained poison, and had Dan's attendants administer it.

sentences.zh: 事覺，帝欲誅之，誕自引咎，懇乞其生。

translations.literal: When the affair came to light the emperor wished to execute him; Dan took the blame upon himself and earnestly begged that his life be spared.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed the emperor meant to put him to death; Dan accepted the blame and pleaded earnestly for his brother's life.

sentences.zh: 帝亦以其父老，杖修百餘，黜為平城民。

translations.literal: The emperor also, because his father was old, had Xiu beaten more than a hundred strokes and demoted him to commoner status at Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, mindful that Xiu's father was aged, had Xiu beaten more than a hundred times and reduced him to a commoner of Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 及誕、熙繼卒，幽后尋廢，聿亦擯棄，馮氏遂衰。

translations.literal: When Dan and Xi died in succession, the Deposed Empress was soon removed, Yu was also cast aside, and the Feng clan thus declined.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan and Xi died one after another, the Deposed Empress was soon cast out, Yu was cast aside as well, and the Feng clan waned.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，魏以彭城王勰為司徒。

translations.literal: On guihai, Wei appointed Prince Xie of Pengcheng as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Wei made Prince Xie of Pengcheng Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 陳顯達與魏元英戰，屢破之。

translations.literal: Chen Xianda fought Yuan Ying of Wei and repeatedly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianda battled Yuan Ying of Wei and routed him again and again.

sentences.zh: 攻馬圈城四十日，城中食盡，啖死人肉及樹皮。

translations.literal: He besieged the city of Maquan for forty days; food in the city was exhausted and they ate the flesh of the dead and tree bark.
translations.idiomatic: He invested Maquan for forty days until the city's food was gone and the defenders ate the flesh of the dead and tree bark.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，魏人突圍走，斬獲千計。

translations.literal: On guiyou, the men of Wei broke out of the encirclement and fled; those killed and captured numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou the Wei forces broke out and fled; the Qi army killed and captured thousands.

sentences.zh: 顯達入城，將士競取城中絹，遂不窮追。

translations.literal: Xianda entered the city; officers and soldiers vied to seize the silk in the city, and so they did not pursue to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda entered the city, but his troops scrambled for the silk stored there and therefore did not press the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 顯達又遣軍主莊丘黑進擊南鄉，拔之。

translations.literal: Xianda also sent the army commander Zhuangqiu He to advance against Nanxiang and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda also sent the army commander Zhuangqiu He against Nanxiang and took it.

sentences.zh: 魏主謂任城王澄曰：「顯達侵擾，朕不親行，無以制之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor of Wei said to Prince Cheng of Ren: "Xianda is raiding and harassing us; if I do not go in person, there is no way to bring him under control."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor said to Prince Cheng of Ren, "Xianda is pressing our borders; unless I take the field myself, there is no holding him in check."

sentences.zh: 三月，庚辰，魏主發洛陽，命於烈居守，以右衛將軍宋弁兼祠部尚書，攝七兵事以佐之。

translations.literal: In the third month, on gengchen, the Emperor of Wei set out from Luoyang, ordered Yu Lie to remain and guard the capital, and appointed General of the Right Guard Song Bian as concurrent Minister of Rites and acting overseer of the seven military offices to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengchen, the Wei emperor left Luoyang, left Yu Lie to guard the capital, and made General of the Right Guard Song Bian concurrent Minister of Rites with acting charge of military affairs to assist him.

sentences.zh: 弁精勤吏治，恩遇亞於李沖。

translations.literal: Bian was diligent and exacting in civil administration; his favor ranked second only to Li Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was meticulous in civil administration, and the favor shown him was second only to Li Chong.

sentences.zh: 癸未，魏主至梁城。

translations.literal: On guimou, the Emperor of Wei arrived at Liangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On guimou the Wei emperor reached Liangcheng.

sentences.zh: 崔慧景攻魏順陽，順陽太守清河張烈固守；

translations.literal: Cui Jingjing attacked Shunyang of Wei; the governor of Shunyang, Zhang Lie of Qinghe, held firm;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Jingjing attacked Wei's Shunyang, but the governor Zhang Lie of Qinghe held the city;

sentences.zh: 甲申，魏主遣振威將軍慕容平城將騎五千救之。

translations.literal: On jiashen, the Emperor of Wei sent General Who Quells Might Murong Pingcheng with five thousand horsemen to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen the Wei emperor sent General Who Quells Might Murong Pingcheng with five thousand cavalry to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 自魏主有疾，彭城王勰常居中侍醫藥，晝夜不離左右，飲食必先嘗而後進，蓬首垢面，衣不解帶。

translations.literal: From the time the Emperor of Wei fell ill, Prince Xie of Pengcheng constantly attended him within the palace with medicines, day and night never leaving his side, always tasting food and drink before it was served, with unkempt hair and a grimy face, his garments never unfastened.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since the Wei emperor fell ill, Prince Xie of Pengcheng had stayed at his side within the palace tending his medicines, never leaving him day or night, tasting every meal before it was served, his hair unkempt, his face unwashed, his belt never loosened.

sentences.zh: 帝久疾多忿，近侍失指，動欲誅斬。

translations.literal: The emperor, long ill and prone to anger, would find fault with attendants close at hand and at every turn wish to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, long ill and quick to rage, would seize on the slightest slip by those near him and at once want them put to death.

sentences.zh: 勰承顏伺間，多所匡救。

translations.literal: Xie would read his expression and watch for openings, and in many cases set matters right and save lives.
translations.idiomatic: Xie read his mood and seized every chance to intervene, saving many from execution.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以勰為使持節、都督中外諸軍事。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Xie was made bearer of the staff of authority and commander-in-chief of all armies at home and abroad.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Xie was appointed bearer of the imperial staff and supreme commander of all forces within and beyond the borders.

sentences.zh: 勰辭曰：「臣侍疾無暇，安能治軍！

translations.literal: Xie declined, saying: "Your servant attends the illness and has no leisure—how can he command armies!
translations.idiomatic: Xie declined, saying, "I am wholly occupied nursing Your Majesty's illness—how can I command armies!

sentences.zh: 願更請一王，使總軍要，臣得專心醫藥。」

translations.literal: I beg that another prince be requested to take overall charge of military affairs, so that your servant may devote himself solely to medicines."
translations.idiomatic: Please appoint another prince to hold overall military command so that I may devote myself entirely to your care."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「侍疾、治軍，皆憑於汝。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Nursing the illness and commanding the armies both depend on you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Both my nursing and the armies depend on you.

sentences.zh: 吾病如此，深慮不濟；

translations.literal: My illness is such that I deeply fear it will not succeed;
translations.idiomatic: My illness is so grave that I deeply fear I shall not recover;

sentences.zh: 安六軍、保社稷者，捨汝而誰！

translations.literal: to settle the six armies and preserve the altars of state—apart from you, who else!
translations.idiomatic: to steady the six armies and preserve the realm—who but you!

sentences.zh: 何容方更請人以違心寄乎！」

translations.literal: How could I now ask for another man and go against the trust of my heart!"
translations.idiomatic: How could I now ask for someone else and betray the trust I place in you!"

sentences.zh: 丁酉，魏主至馬圈，命荊州刺史廣陽王嘉斷均口，邀齊兵歸路。

translations.literal: On dingyou, the Emperor of Wei arrived at Maquan and ordered the governor of Jing Province, Prince Jia of Guangyang, to cut off the Junkou pass and intercept the Qi army's line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou the Wei emperor reached Maquan and ordered the governor of Jing, Prince Jia of Guangyang, to block the Jun outlet and cut off the Qi army's retreat.

sentences.zh: 嘉，建之子也。

translations.literal: Jia was the son of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Jia was the son of Jian.

sentences.zh: 陳顯達引兵渡水西，據鷹子山築城；

translations.literal: Chen Xianda led his army across to the west of the river and built a fort on Mount Yingzi;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianda led his troops west across the river and fortified Eagle Peak;

sentences.zh: 人情沮恐，與魏戰，屢敗。

translations.literal: morale was dejected and fearful; in battle with Wei they were repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: morale sank in fear, and in battle with Wei they were beaten again and again.

sentences.zh: 魏武衛將軍元嵩免冑陷陳，將士隨之，齊兵大敗。

translations.literal: The Wei Martial Guard General Yuan Song removed his helmet and plunged into the battle line; officers and soldiers followed him, and the Qi army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's Martial Guard General Yuan Song cast off his helmet and charged into the enemy ranks; his men followed, and the Qi army was routed.

sentences.zh: 嵩，澄之弟也。

translations.literal: Song was the younger brother of Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Song was Cheng's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，夜，軍主崔恭祖、胡松以烏布幔盛顯達，數人擔之，間道自分磧山出均水口南走。

translations.literal: On wuxu, at night, the army commanders Cui Gongzu and Hu Song wrapped Xianda in a black-cloth canopy; several men carried him by a hidden path from Mount Fenqi south out through the Jun outlet and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, by night, army commanders Cui Gongzu and Hu Song wrapped Xianda in a black cloth litter; several men bore him along a secret route south from Mount Fenqi through the Jun outlet to escape.

sentences.zh: 己亥，魏收顯達軍資億計，班賜將士，追奔至漢水而還。

translations.literal: On jihai, Wei gathered Xianda's military stores, reckoned in the hundreds of millions, distributed rewards among officers and soldiers, pursued the fugitives to the Han River, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Wei seized Xianda's supplies, worth hundreds of millions, rewarded the troops, pursued the fugitives to the Han River, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 左軍將軍張千戰死，士卒死者三萬餘人。

translations.literal: The Left Army General Zhang Qian died in battle; soldiers killed numbered more than thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Left Army General Zhang Qian was killed in battle, and more than thirty thousand soldiers died.

sentences.zh: 顯達之北伐，軍入汋均口。

translations.literal: When Xianda marched north, his army entered the Zhuojun pass.
translations.idiomatic: On Xianda's northern campaign his army entered the Zhuo-Jun outlet.

sentences.zh: 廣平馮道根說顯達曰：「汋均水迅急，易進難退；

translations.literal: Feng Daogen of Guangping urged Xianda, saying: "The Zhuojun waters run swift and violent; it is easy to advance and hard to retreat;
translations.idiomatic: Feng Daogen of Guangping warned Xianda, "The Zhuo-Jun current runs fast; it is easy to go in and hard to get out;

sentences.zh: 魏若守隘，則首尾俱急。

translations.literal: if Wei holds the defile, then head and tail will both be in peril.
translations.idiomatic: if Wei holds the pass, you will be trapped at both ends.

sentences.zh: 不如悉棄船於酇城，陸道步進，列營相次，鼓行而前，破之必矣。」

translations.literal: It would be better to abandon all the boats at Zheng and advance by land, with camps set out in succession, marching forward to the beat of drums—victory is certain."
translations.idiomatic: Better to leave every boat at Zheng and march overland, camp after camp in line, advancing to the drumbeat—you are sure to break them."

sentences.zh: 顯達不從。

translations.literal: Xianda did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda would not listen.

sentences.zh: 道根以私屬從軍，及顯達夜走，軍人不知山路，道根每及險要，輒停馬指示之，眾賴以全。

translations.literal: Daogen had followed the army as a private retainer; when Xianda fled by night the soldiers did not know the mountain paths, but at every dangerous point Daogen would halt his horse and point the way, and the force owed its survival to him.
translations.idiomatic: Daogen had come along as a private follower; when Xianda fled by night the troops did not know the mountain trails, but at every dangerous pass Daogen would stop his horse and show the way, and the army owed its escape to him.

sentences.zh: 詔以道根為汋均口戍副。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Daogen deputy warden of the Zhuojun pass.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Daogen deputy commander of the Zhuo-Jun garrison.

sentences.zh: 顯達素有威名，至是大損。

translations.literal: Xianda had long enjoyed a formidable reputation, but on this occasion it suffered a great blow.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda's name had long carried weight, but now it was gravely diminished.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞范岫奏免顯達官，顯達亦自表解職；

translations.literal: The Censor-in-Chief Fan Xiu memorialized that Xianda be removed from office, and Xianda also submitted a memorial requesting to resign;
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Fan Xiu memorialized to strip Xianda of his posts, and Xianda too asked to resign;

sentences.zh: 皆不許，更以顯達為江州刺史。

translations.literal: neither was granted; instead Xianda was reassigned as governor of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: both pleas were denied, and Xianda was made governor of Jiang Province instead.

sentences.zh: 崔慧景亦棄順陽走還。

translations.literal: Cui Jingjing also abandoned Shunyang and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Jingjing likewise abandoned Shunyang and retreated.

sentences.zh: 庚子，魏主疾甚，北還，至谷塘原，謂司徒勰曰：「後宮久乖陰德，吾死之後，可賜自盡，葬以后禮，庶免馮門之丑。」

translations.literal: On gengzi, the Emperor of Wei was gravely ill and turned north; when he reached Gutang Plain he said to Minister of Works Xie: "The inner palace has long violated feminine virtue; after my death you may grant her suicide and bury her with empress's rites, so as to avoid the shame of the Feng clan."
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the Wei emperor was critically ill and headed north; at Gutang Plain he told Minister of Works Xie, "The inner palace has long betrayed feminine virtue; after I die, grant her death and bury her with empress's honors, lest the Feng clan's disgrace spread further."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「吾病益惡，殆必不起。

translations.literal: He also said: "My illness grows worse; I surely shall not rise again.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "My illness grows worse; I will surely not recover.

sentences.zh: 雖摧破顯達，而天下未平，嗣子幼弱，社稷所倚，唯在於汝。

translations.literal: Though we have shattered Xianda, the realm is not yet settled, the heir is young and weak, and upon whom the altars of state must rely—only you.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xianda is broken, the realm is not yet at peace, the heir is young and frail, and the altars of state rest on you alone.

sentences.zh: 霍子孟、諸葛孔明以異姓受顧托，況汝親賢，可不勉之！」

translations.literal: Huo Zimeng and Zhuge Kongming received the dying charge though of different surnames—how much more should you, close kin and worthy, exert yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: Huo Guang and Zhuge Liang took the dying charge though they were not of the imperial clan—how much more must you, my close kin and worthy man, strive!"

sentences.zh: 勰泣曰：「布衣之士，猶為知己畢命；

translations.literal: Xie wept and said: "Even a man in plain cloth will give his life for one who knows him;
translations.idiomatic: Xie wept and said, "Even a commoner will die for one who knows his worth;

sentences.zh: 況臣托靈先帝，依陛下之末光乎！

translations.literal: how much more your servant, who owes his spirit to the late emperor and leans upon Your Majesty's last radiance!
translations.idiomatic: how much more I, who owe my being to the late emperor and live in Your Majesty's reflected light!

sentences.zh: 但臣以至親，久參機要，寵靈輝赫，海內莫及；

translations.literal: Yet your servant, as the closest kin, has long shared in the secrets of state; favor and honor blaze so brightly that none within the seas can match it;
translations.idiomatic: Yet I am your closest kin and have long held the reins of power; my favor blazes so high that none under heaven can match it;

sentences.zh: 所以敢受而不辭，正恃陛下日月之明，恕臣忘退之過耳。

translations.literal: the reason I dared accept and did not decline was precisely that I relied on Your Majesty's sun-and-moon brightness to forgive my fault of forgetting to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: I dared accept only because I trusted in Your Majesty's brilliance to forgive my failure to step back in time.

sentences.zh: 今復任以元宰，總握機政；

translations.literal: Now to be appointed again as chief minister and to grasp all affairs of state;
translations.idiomatic: Now to be named chief minister and hold every lever of state;

sentences.zh: 震主之聲，取罪必矣。

translations.literal: a renown that shakes the ruler—offense is certain.
translations.idiomatic: a name that overshadows the throne—guilt is inevitable.

sentences.zh: 昔周公大聖，成王至明，猶不免疑，而況臣乎！

translations.literal: In old times the Duke of Zhou was supremely sage and King Cheng supremely enlightened, yet suspicion could not be avoided—how much more your servant!
translations.idiomatic: Even the Duke of Zhou, greatest of sages, and King Cheng, brightest of kings, could not escape suspicion—how much more I!

sentences.zh: 如此，則陛下愛臣，更為未盡始終之美。」

translations.literal: In this way Your Majesty's love for your servant would fall short of the beauty of seeing things through from start to finish."
translations.idiomatic: That way Your Majesty's love for me would fail to reach a graceful end."

sentences.zh: 帝默然久之，曰：「詳思汝言，理實難奪。」

translations.literal: The emperor was silent a long while, then said: "I have pondered your words in detail; the reasoning is hard to overturn."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was silent a long while, then said, "I have weighed your words carefully; the logic is hard to refute."

sentences.zh: 乃手詔太子曰：「汝叔父勰，清規懋賞，與白雲俱潔；

translations.literal: He then wrote a hand edict to the crown prince: "Your uncle Xie keeps pure standards and lofty merit, clean as the white clouds;
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote a personal edict to the crown prince: "Your uncle Xie holds himself to pure standards and high merit, spotless as white clouds;

sentences.zh: 厭榮捨紱，以松竹為心。

translations.literal: weary of glory, he casts off rank and takes pine and bamboo as his heart.
translations.idiomatic: weary of glory, he would cast off rank and keep pine and bamboo in his heart.

sentences.zh: 吾少與綢繆，未忍睽離。

translations.literal: From youth I have been bound to him in close friendship and cannot bear to part.
translations.idiomatic: We have been close since youth, and I cannot bear to part from him.

sentences.zh: 百年之後，其聽勰辭蟬捨冕，遂其沖挹之性。」

translations.literal: After a hundred years, let him hear Xie's request to lay down the cicada and crown and fulfill his retiring nature."
translations.idiomatic: After I am gone, let Xie lay down rank and crown and live out his modest nature."

sentences.zh: 以侍中、護軍將軍北海王詳為司空，鎮南將軍王肅為尚書令，鎮南大將軍廣陽王嘉為左僕射，尚書宋弁為吏部尚書，與侍中、太尉禧、尚書右僕射，尚書宋弁為吏部尚書，與侍中、太尉禧、尚書右僕射澄等六人輔政。

translations.literal: He appointed Palace Attendant and General Who Guards the Army Prince Xiang of Beihai as Minister of Works, General Who Guards the South Wang Su as Minister of the Secretariat, Grand General Who Guards the South Prince Jia of Guangyang as Left Vice Minister, and Minister Song Bian as Minister of Personnel; together with Palace Attendant and Grand Marshal Xi, Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat, Minister Song Bian as Minister of Personnel, together with Palace Attendant and Grand Marshal Xi, Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat Cheng, and others—six men to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: He named Palace Attendant and General Who Guards the Army Prince Xiang of Beihai Minister of Works, General Who Guards the South Wang Su Minister of the Secretariat, Grand General Who Guards the South Prince Jia of Guangyang Left Vice Minister, and Minister Song Bian Minister of Personnel; together with Palace Attendant and Grand Marshal Xi, Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat, Minister Song Bian as Minister of Personnel, together with Palace Attendant and Grand Marshal Xi, Right Vice Minister Cheng, and others—six men to form the regency.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙午朔，殂於谷塘原。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the new moon day bingwu, he died at Gutang Plain.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the first day of the fourth month (bingwu), he died at Gutang Plain.

sentences.zh: 高祖友愛諸弟，始終無間。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu cherished his younger brothers and from first to last there was no breach between them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu loved his younger brothers warmly, and their bond never broke.

sentences.zh: 嘗從容謂咸陽王禧等曰：「我後子孫解逅不肖，汝等觀望，可輔則輔之，不可輔則取之，勿為它人有也。」

translations.literal: He once said calmly to Prince Xi of Xianyang and the others: "If my later descendants chance to be unworthy, you are to observe: if they can be assisted, assist them; if they cannot, take the realm—do not let another have it."
translations.idiomatic: He once told Prince Xi of Xianyang and the others calmly, "If my descendants prove unworthy, watch them: assist them if you can; if not, take the throne yourselves—do not let outsiders have it."

sentences.zh: 親任賢能，從善如流，精勤庶務，朝夕不倦。

translations.literal: He personally entrusted the worthy and able, followed good counsel as flowing water, and was diligent in all affairs of state, never weary from morning to night.
translations.idiomatic: He personally employed the worthy, followed good counsel readily, and labored at state affairs from dawn to dusk without tiring.

sentences.zh: 常曰：「人主患不能處心公平，推誠於物。

translations.literal: He often said: "What a ruler should fear is inability to set his heart on fairness and extend sincerity to all things.
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "A ruler's trouble is failing to keep a fair mind and extend sincerity to all.

sentences.zh: 能是二者，則胡、越之人皆可使如兄弟矣。」

translations.literal: If he can do these two things, then even Hu and Yue peoples can be made like brothers."
translations.idiomatic: Master these two, and even Hu and Yue peoples can be made as close as brothers."

sentences.zh: 用法雖嚴，於大臣無所容貸，然人有小過，常多闊略。

translations.literal: Though his application of law was strict and he showed no indulgence toward great ministers, yet when men had small faults he often overlooked them broadly.
translations.idiomatic: Though he enforced the law strictly and showed no mercy to great ministers, he often overlooked petty faults.

sentences.zh: 嘗於食中得蟲，又左右進羹誤傷帝手，皆笑而赦之。

translations.literal: Once he found a worm in his food, and again attendants bringing soup accidentally hurt the emperor's hand—he laughed and pardoned them in both cases.
translations.idiomatic: Once he found a worm in his food; another time attendants spilling soup scalded his hand—in both cases he laughed and pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 天地五郊、宗廟二分之祭，未嘗不身親其禮。

translations.literal: At sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, the five suburban altars, and the temple rites at the two equinoxes, he never failed to perform the ceremonies in person.
translations.idiomatic: For sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, the five suburban rites, and the ancestral temple observances at the equinoxes, he always performed the rites himself.

sentences.zh: 每出巡遊及用兵，有司奏修道路，帝輒曰：「粗修橋樑，通車馬而已，勿去草鏟令平也。」

translations.literal: Whenever he went out on tour or on campaign and the offices reported on repairing roads, the emperor would say: "Roughly repair bridges so that carts and horses may pass—that is enough; do not clear away grass and level the ground."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he toured or campaigned and officials proposed road repairs, he would say, "Patch the bridges enough for carts and horses—that is all; do not strip the grass and level the ground."

sentences.zh: 在淮南行兵，如在境內，禁士卒無得踐傷粟稻；

translations.literal: When campaigning in Huainan he treated it as within his own borders and forbade soldiers to tread upon or harm grain and rice;
translations.idiomatic: On campaign in Huainan he treated the land as his own domain and forbade troops to trample grain;

sentences.zh: 或伐民樹以供軍用，皆留絹償之。

translations.literal: if trees of the people were cut to supply the army, silk was always left in compensation.
translations.idiomatic: if trees were felled for the army, silk was left to pay for them.

sentences.zh: 宮室非不得已不修，衣弊，浣濯而服之，鞍勒用鐵木而已。

translations.literal: Palaces were not repaired unless unavoidable; when garments were worn out he washed them and wore them again; saddle and bridle were of ironwood only.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired palaces only when he must; worn clothes he washed and wore again; saddle and bridle were plain ironwood.

sentences.zh: 幼多力善射，能以指彈碎羊骨，射禽獸無不命中；

translations.literal: In youth he was very strong and skilled at archery; he could snap sheep bones with a flick of the finger, and in shooting birds and beasts he never missed;
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was powerful and skilled with the bow; he could snap sheep bones with a flick of his finger, and never missed his mark hunting birds and beasts;

sentences.zh: 及年十五，遂不復畋獵。

translations.literal: but from the age of fifteen he never hunted again.
translations.idiomatic: but from the age of fifteen he gave up hunting altogether.

sentences.zh: 常謂史官曰：「時事不可以不直書。

translations.literal: He often told the historiographers: "Current affairs must be written straight and not concealed.
translations.idiomatic: He often told the historiographers, "Current affairs must be recorded truthfully.

sentences.zh: 人君威福在己，無能制之者；

translations.literal: A ruler's authority and blessings rest in his own hands, and none can restrain him;
translations.idiomatic: A ruler holds all power in his own hands, and none can check him;

sentences.zh: 若史策復不書其惡，將何所畏忌邪！」

translations.literal: if the historical records again do not write his evils, what will he have to fear!"
translations.idiomatic: if the histories do not record his wrongs, what will he have left to fear?"

sentences.zh: 彭城王勰與任城王澄謀，以陳顯達去尚未遠，恐其覆相掩逼，乃秘不發喪，徙御臥輿，唯二王與左右數人知之。

translations.literal: Prince Xie of Pengcheng and Prince Cheng of Ren plotted together: because Chen Xianda had departed but was not yet far, they feared he might turn back and press them from behind, and so they concealed the death and did not announce mourning, moving the emperor into the traveling couch—only the two princes and a few attendants knew.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xie of Pengcheng and Prince Cheng of Ren agreed that with Chen Xianda not yet far off he might turn back and trap them, so they kept the death secret, moved the emperor into the traveling litter, and told only the two princes and a handful of attendants.

sentences.zh: 勰出入神色無異，奉膳，進藥，可決外奏，一如平日。

translations.literal: Xie came and went with unchanged expression, presented food, administered medicine, and decided memorials from outside just as on ordinary days.
translations.idiomatic: Xie came and went with an unchanged face, served meals, gave medicine, and ruled on outside memorials exactly as before.

sentences.zh: 數日，至宛城，夜，進臥輿於郡聽事，得加棺斂，還載臥輿內，外莫有知者。

translations.literal: After several days they reached Wancheng; at night they brought the traveling couch into the commandery hall, were able to place the body in the coffin and perform the encoffining, then returned it to the couch—none outside knew.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later they reached Wancheng; that night they brought the litter into the commandery hall, coffined the body, and returned it to the litter—no one outside knew.

sentences.zh: 遣中書舍人張儒奉詔征太子；

translations.literal: They sent Palace Secretariat Attendant Zhang Ru with an edict to summon the crown prince;
translations.idiomatic: They sent Palace Secretariat Attendant Zhang Ru with an edict to summon the crown prince;

sentences.zh: 密以凶問告留守於烈。

translations.literal: and secretly informed Yu Lie, who had remained to guard the capital, of the death.
translations.idiomatic: and secretly told Yu Lie, left behind in the capital, of the death.

sentences.zh: 烈處分行留，舉止無變。

translations.literal: Lie disposed affairs and carried out his duties; his bearing showed no change.
translations.idiomatic: Lie carried on the administration without any change in manner.

sentences.zh: 太子至魯陽，遇梓宮，乃發喪；

translations.literal: When the crown prince reached Luyang he met the bier and only then announced mourning;
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince reached Luyang he met the bier and only then proclaimed mourning;

sentences.zh: 丁巳，即位，大赦。

translations.literal: On dingsi he took the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi he ascended the throne and declared a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 彭城王勰跪授遣敕數紙。

translations.literal: Prince Xie of Pengcheng knelt and handed over several sheets of the dying charge.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xie of Pengcheng knelt and presented the several sheets of the dying charge.

sentences.zh: 東宮官屬多疑勰有異志，密防之，而勰推誠盡禮，卒無間隙。

translations.literal: The officials of the Eastern Palace mostly suspected that Xie harbored a different intent and secretly guarded against him, but Xie extended sincerity and performed every rite, and in the end there was no opening.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace staff mostly suspected Xie of ulterior designs and watched him in secret, but he acted with full sincerity and courtesy, and in the end they found no fault.

sentences.zh: 咸陽王禧至魯陽，留城外以察其變。

translations.literal: Prince Xi of Xianyang reached Luyang but remained outside the walls to observe how matters developed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xi of Xianyang reached Luyang but stayed outside the walls to watch for trouble.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃入，謂勰曰：「汝此行不唯勤勞，亦實危險。」

translations.literal: After a long while he entered and said to Xie: "On this journey you were not only laborious but truly in peril."
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he entered and told Xie, "This journey was not only arduous—it was truly dangerous."

sentences.zh: 勰曰：「兄年長識高，故知有夷險；

translations.literal: Xie said: "Elder brother, you are older and wiser, and therefore knew there was peril and ease;
translations.idiomatic: Xie said, "You are older and wiser, brother, so you knew danger from safety;

sentences.zh: 彥和握蛇騎虎，不覺艱難。」

translations.literal: Yanhe held a serpent and rode a tiger and did not feel the hardship."
translations.idiomatic: Yanhe held a serpent and rode a tiger and never felt the strain."

sentences.zh: 禧曰：「汝恨吾後至耳。」

translations.literal: Xi said: "You resent that I arrived late, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "You only resent that I came late."

sentences.zh: 勰等以高祖遺詔，賜馮后死。

translations.literal: Xie and the others, following Emperor Gaozu's dying charge, granted Empress Feng death.
translations.idiomatic: Following Emperor Gaozu's dying charge, Xie and the others ordered Empress Feng to die.

sentences.zh: 北海王詳使長秋卿白整入授后藥，后走呼，不肯飲，曰：「官豈有此，是諸王輩殺我耳！」

translations.literal: Prince Xiang of Beihai sent the Director of the Long Autumn Bai Zheng to enter and present poison to the empress; she ran about shouting and refused to drink, saying: "How could the court have such a thing—it is those princes who are killing me!"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiang of Beihai sent Director of the Long Autumn Bai Zheng in with poison for the empress; she ran about crying and would not drink, saying, "The court would never do this—it is those princes killing me!"

sentences.zh: 整執持強之，乃飲藥而卒。

translations.literal: Zheng seized and forced her, and she drank the drug and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng seized her and forced the draught down; she drank and died.

sentences.zh: 喪至洛城南，咸陽王禧等知后審死，相視曰：「設無遺詔，我兄弟亦當決策去之；

translations.literal: When the funeral procession reached south of Luoyang, Prince Xi of Xianyang and the others, knowing the empress was truly dead, looked at one another and said: "Even without the dying charge, we brothers should have decided to remove her;
translations.idiomatic: When the funeral reached south of Luoyang, Prince Xi of Xianyang and the others, knowing the empress was truly dead, looked at one another and said, "Even without the dying charge we brothers would have had to remove her;

sentences.zh: 豈可令失行婦人宰制天下，殺我輩也！」

translations.literal: how could we let a woman of loose conduct rule the realm and kill us all!"
translations.idiomatic: how could we let a woman of loose conduct rule the realm and slaughter us!"

sentences.zh: 謚曰幽皇后。

translations.literal: She was given the posthumous title Deposed Empress.
translations.idiomatic: She was given the posthumous title Deposed Empress.

sentences.zh: 五月，癸亥，加撫軍大將軍始安王遙光開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on guihai, Grand General Who Pacifies the Army Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an was given the additional title of Bearer of the Insignia Equal to the Three Dukes with an office equal to a ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on guihai, Grand General Who Pacifies the Army Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an was granted Bearer of the Insignia Equal to the Three Dukes with ministerial standing.

sentences.zh: 丙申，魏葬孝文帝於長陵，廟號高祖。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Wei buried Emperor Xiaowen at Changling; his temple name was Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Wei buried Emperor Xiaowen at Changling with the temple name Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 魏世宗欲以彭城王勰為相；

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong of Wei wished to make Prince Xie of Pengcheng chief minister;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong of Wei wished to make Prince Xie of Pengcheng his chief minister;

sentences.zh: 勰屢陳遺旨，請遂素懷，帝對之悲慟。

translations.literal: Xie repeatedly cited the dying charge and begged to fulfill his lifelong wish; the emperor faced him with grief and anguish.
translations.idiomatic: Xie repeatedly cited the dying charge and asked to honor his lifelong wish; the emperor wept before him in grief.

sentences.zh: 勰懇請不已，乃以勰為使持節、侍中、都督冀、定等七州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、定州刺史。

translations.literal: When Xie's earnest pleas did not cease, he was appointed bearer of the staff of authority, Palace Attendant, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the seven provinces including Ji and Ding, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Bearer of the Insignia Equal to the Three Dukes with an office equal to a ministry, and governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: As Xie's pleas would not end, he was named bearer of the imperial staff, Palace Attendant, commander-in-chief of the seven provinces including Ji and Ding, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Bearer of the Insignia Equal to the Three Dukes, and governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 勰猶固辭，帝不許，乃之官。

translations.literal: Xie still firmly declined, but the emperor would not allow it, and he then went to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Xie still refused, but the emperor would not hear of it, and he took up his post.

sentences.zh: 魏任城王澄以王肅羈旅，位加己上，意頗不平。

translations.literal: Prince Cheng of Ren of Wei, because Wang Su was a man dwelling abroad whose rank stood above his own, was somewhat displeased in his mind.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Cheng of Ren resented that Wang Su, a man living in exile, held rank above his own.

sentences.zh: 會齊人降者嚴叔懋告肅謀逃還江南，澄輒禁止肅，表稱謀叛；

translations.literal: It happened that Yan Shumao, a man of Qi who had surrendered, reported that Su plotted to flee back to the lands south of the Yangtze; Cheng at once placed Su under restraint and memorialized that he plotted rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: A Qi defector named Yan Shumao reported that Su planned to flee back to the south; Cheng at once detained Su and memorialized that he plotted rebellion;

sentences.zh: 案驗無實。

translations.literal: investigation found no substance to the charge.
translations.idiomatic: investigation found no truth in the charge.

sentences.zh: 咸陽王禧等奏澄擅禁宰輔，免官還第，尋出為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Prince Xi of Xianyang and others memorialized that Cheng had on his own authority restrained a chief minister; he was removed from office and returned to his residence, and soon after was sent out as governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xi of Xianyang and others memorialized that Cheng had detained a chief minister on his own authority; he was stripped of office and sent home, then soon appointed governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 六月，戊辰，魏追尊皇妣高氏為文昭皇后，配饗高祖，增修舊塚，號終寧陵。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on wuchen, Wei posthumously honored the emperor's mother of the Gao clan as Empress Wenzhao, paired in sacrifice with Gaozu, enlarged and repaired her former tomb, and named it Zhongning Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on wuchen, Wei posthumously honored the emperor's mother Lady Gao as Empress Wenzhao, enshrined her beside Gaozu, enlarged her old tomb, and named it Zhongning Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 追賜後父颺爵勃海公，謚曰敬，以其嫡孫猛襲爵；

translations.literal: The empress's father Yang was posthumously given the title Duke of Bohai with the posthumous epithet Respectful, and his legitimate grandson Meng inherited the title;
translations.idiomatic: The empress's father Yang was posthumously made Duke of Bohai with the epithet Respectful, and his legitimate grandson Meng inherited the title;

sentences.zh: 封後兄肇為平原公，肇弟顯為澄城公；

translations.literal: the empress's elder brother Zhao was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan and Zhao's younger brother Xian as Duke of Chengcheng;
translations.idiomatic: the empress's elder brother Zhao was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan and Zhao's younger brother Xian as Duke of Chengcheng;

sentences.zh: 三人同日受封。

translations.literal: all three received enfeoffment on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: all three were enfeoffed on the same day.

sentences.zh: 魏主素未識諸舅，始賜衣幘引見，皆惶懼失措；

translations.literal: The Emperor of Wei had never known his maternal uncles; when he first granted them garments and caps and summoned them to audience, all were fearful and at a loss;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor had never met his maternal uncles; when he first gave them robes and caps and received them in audience, they were all terrified and at a loss;

sentences.zh: 數日之間，富貴赫奕。

translations.literal: within a few days their wealth and glory blazed brilliantly.
translations.idiomatic: within days their wealth and glory blazed beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，戊申，魏用高祖遺詔，三夫人以下皆遣還家。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on wushen, Wei followed Emperor Gaozu's dying charge and sent home all consorts from the rank of Third Lady and below.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, on wushen, Wei carried out Gaozu's dying charge and sent home every consort from Third Lady downward.

sentences.zh: 帝自在東宮，不好學，唯嬉戲無度；

translations.literal: The emperor, from the time he was in the Eastern Palace, did not love learning and only played without measure;
translations.idiomatic: From his days in the Eastern Palace the emperor disliked study and played without restraint;

sentences.zh: 性重澀少言。

translations.literal: his nature was grave, slow, and sparing of speech.
translations.idiomatic: his nature was grave and taciturn.

sentences.zh: 及即位，不與朝士相接，專親信宦官及左右御刀、應敕等。

translations.literal: When he took the throne he did not meet with court gentlemen but trusted only eunuchs and attendants such as the imperial sword-bearers at his side and those who answered edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned he shunned court officials and trusted only eunuchs and personal attendants such as the imperial sword-bearers and edict runners.

sentences.zh: 是時，揚州刺史始安王遙光、尚書令徐孝嗣、右僕射江祏、右將軍蕭坦之、侍中江祀，衛尉劉暄更直內省，分日帖敕。

translations.literal: At this time the governor of Yang Province Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an, Minister of the Secretariat Xu Xiaosi, Right Vice Minister Jiang Shi, Right General Xiao Tanzhi, Palace Attendant Jiang Si, and Commandant of the Guard Liu Xuan took turns on duty within the inner palace, dividing the days to affix edicts.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Governor of Yang Province Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an, Minister of the Secretariat Xu Xiaosi, Right Vice Minister Jiang Shi, Right General Xiao Tanzhi, Palace Attendant Jiang Si, and Commandant of the Guard Liu Xuan rotated duty in the inner palace, each affixing edicts on his assigned day.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史蕭衍聞之，謂從舅錄事參軍范陽張弘策曰：「一國三公猶不堪，況六貴同朝，勢必相圖，亂將作矣。

translations.literal: When Xiao Yan, governor of Yong Province, heard of this he said to his mother's sister's son, the recording affairs officer Zhang Hongce of Fanyang: "Even three dukes in one state are hard to bear—how much more six nobles together at court; they are bound to plot against one another, and disorder is about to break out.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Yan, governor of Yong Province, heard this he told his cousin on his mother's side, recording affairs officer Zhang Hongce of Fanyang, "Even three dukes in one state are unbearable—how much more six nobles at court together; they are bound to plot against one another, and turmoil is coming.

sentences.zh: 避禍圖福，無如此州，但諸弟在都，恐罹世患，當更與益州圖之耳。」

translations.literal: To avoid calamity and seek fortune there is no place like this province, but my younger brothers are in the capital and may suffer the troubles of the age—we must also make plans with Yi Province."
translations.idiomatic: To escape disaster and seek fortune there is no better province, but my younger brothers are in the capital and may be caught in the coming storm—we must also plan with Yi Province."

sentences.zh: 乃密與弘策修武備，它人皆不得預謀。

translations.literal: He then secretly with Hongce prepared military defenses; no others were allowed to share in the planning.
translations.idiomatic: He then secretly prepared defenses with Hongce; no one else was let into the planning.

sentences.zh: 招聚驍勇以萬數，多伐材竹，沉之檀溪，積茅如岡阜，皆不之用。

translations.literal: He gathered fierce warriors by the tens of thousands, felled much timber and bamboo and sank it in Tan Stream, piled thatch like hillocks—yet used none of it.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited tens of thousands of fierce fighters, felled timber and bamboo in quantity and sank it in Tan Stream, piled thatch like hills—and used none of it yet.

sentences.zh: 中兵參軍東平呂僧珍覺其意，亦私具櫓數百張。

translations.literal: The middle army officer Lü Sengzhen of Dongping perceived his intent and on his own secretly prepared several hundred scaling ladders.
translations.idiomatic: Middle army officer Lü Sengzhen of Dongping sensed his intent and secretly prepared several hundred scaling ladders on his own.

sentences.zh: 先是，僧珍為羽林監，徐孝嗣欲引置其府，僧珍知孝嗣不能久，固求從衍。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Sengzhen was supervisor of the Feathered Forest guard, Xu Xiaosi wished to bring him into his bureau; Sengzhen knew Xiaosi could not last long and firmly begged to follow Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Sengzhen was supervisor of the Feathered Forest guard, Xu Xiaosi tried to bring him into his staff; Sengzhen knew Xiaosi would not last and insisted on following Yan.

sentences.zh: 是時，衍兄懿罷益州刺史還，仍行郢州事，衍使弘策說懿曰：「今六貴比肩，人自畫敕，爭權睚眥，理相圖滅。

translations.literal: At this time Yan's elder brother Yi had left the governorship of Yi Province and returned, and was still acting for the affairs of Ying Province; Yan had Hongce persuade Yi, saying: "Now the six nobles stand shoulder to shoulder, each affixing edicts for himself; they contend for power with the grudges of a slit eye—by reason they are bound to plot one another's destruction.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Yan's elder brother Yi had left the governorship of Yi and returned, still acting for Ying Province; Yan had Hongce tell Yi, "Now the six nobles stand side by side, each stamping his own edicts; they fight for power with murderous grudges—they are bound to destroy one another.

sentences.zh: 主上自東宮素無令譽，媟近左右，慓輕忍虐，安肯委政諸公，虛坐主諾！

translations.literal: The sovereign from the Eastern Palace has never had a good reputation; he is familiar with those close at hand, rash, light, and cruel—how would he be willing to entrust government to these lords and sit idly as master of assent!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor has had no good name since the Eastern Palace; he dotes on those near him, is rash, cruel, and light—how would he hand power to these lords and sit idle nodding assent!

sentences.zh: 嫌忌積久，必大行誅戮。

translations.literal: Suspicion and resentment have piled up for long—he is sure to carry out executions on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: Suspicion has built for years—he is sure to launch a great slaughter.

sentences.zh: 始安欲為趙王倫，形跡已見；

translations.literal: Shi'an wishes to be another Prince Lun of Zhao—his traces are already visible;
translations.idiomatic: Shi'an wants to be another Prince Lun of Zhao—his designs are already plain;

sentences.zh: 然性猜量狹，徒為禍階。

translations.literal: yet his nature is suspicious and his measure narrow, and he will only serve as a stepping-stone to disaster.
translations.idiomatic: yet he is suspicious and narrow-minded and will only pave the way to disaster.

sentences.zh: 蕭坦之忌克陵人，徐孝嗣聽人穿鼻，江祏無斷，劉暄闇弱；

translations.literal: Xiao Tanzhi is jealous and overbearing toward men of Ling; Xu Xiaosi listens while men have their noses pierced; Jiang Shi has no decisiveness; Liu Xuan is dim and weak;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Tanzhi is jealous and harsh toward men of Ling; Xu Xiaosi stands by while men are pierced through the nose; Jiang Shi cannot decide; Liu Xuan is dull and weak;

sentences.zh: 一朝禍發，中外土崩，吾兄弟幸守外籓，宜為身計；

translations.literal: When calamity breaks out in a morning, within and without the state will crumble—our brothers are fortunate to hold outer fiefs; we ought to plan for ourselves;
translations.idiomatic: When disaster strikes overnight, court and country will collapse—our brothers are lucky to hold frontier commands; we must look to our own survival;

sentences.zh: 及今猜防未生，當悉召諸弟，恐異時拔足無路矣。

translations.literal: While suspicion and guard have not yet arisen, we should summon all our younger brothers; I fear that at another time there will be no way to pull up our feet and escape.
translations.idiomatic: Before suspicion takes hold, we should summon all our younger brothers—otherwise we may have no way to escape when the time comes.

sentences.zh: 郢州控帶荊、湘，雍州士馬精強，世治則竭誠本朝，世亂則足以匡濟；

translations.literal: Ying Province controls and links Jing and Xiang; Yong Province's soldiers and horses are elite and strong—in an age of order we can devote ourselves utterly to the dynasty, in an age of chaos we can suffice to set things right;
translations.idiomatic: Ying Province commands Jing and Xiang; Yong has elite troops—in peace we can serve the dynasty faithfully, in turmoil we can set the realm right;

sentences.zh: 與時進退，此萬全之策也。

translations.literal: Advancing and retreating with the times—this is a strategy of complete safety.
translations.idiomatic: Moving with the times—that is the safest course of all.

sentences.zh: 若不早圖，後悔無及。」

translations.literal: If we do not plan early, regret will be too late."
translations.idiomatic: If we do not act now, it will be too late for regret."

sentences.zh: 弘策又自說懿曰：「以卿兄弟英武，天下無敵，據郢、雍二州，為百姓請命，廢昏立明，易於反掌，此桓、文之業也。

translations.literal: Hongce then himself persuaded Yi, saying: "With you brothers' heroism and martial prowess, unmatched under Heaven, holding the two provinces of Ying and Yong, pleading for the people, deposing the dark ruler and raising a bright one—it is as easy as turning the palm; this is the achievement of Huan and Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Hongce then pressed Yi himself: "You and your brothers are unmatched in valor; holding Ying and Yong, you could plead for the people, depose a worthless ruler and raise a worthy one—easier than turning your hand. This is work fit for Duke Huan and Duke Wen.

sentences.zh: 勿為豎子所欺，取笑身後。

translations.literal: Do not be deceived by that stripling and become a laughingstock after death.
translations.idiomatic: Do not let that boy fool you and make a fool of yourself for posterity.

sentences.zh: 雍州揣之已熟，願善圖之！」

translations.literal: Yong Province has weighed this thoroughly—may you plan it well!"
translations.idiomatic: Yong Province has thought this through—plan wisely!"

sentences.zh: 懿不從。

translations.literal: Yi did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Yi refused.

sentences.zh: 衍乃迎其弟驃騎外兵參軍偉及西中郎外兵參軍憺至襄陽。

translations.literal: Yan then welcomed his younger brothers Wei, outer army officer under the Cavalry General-in-Chief, and Dan, outer army officer under the Western Commander of the Center, to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yan then brought his younger brothers Wei (outer army officer under the Cavalry General-in-Chief) and Dan (outer army officer under the Western Commander of the Center) to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 初，高宗雖顧命群公，而多寄腹心在江祏兄弟。

translations.literal: Initially, though Gaozong had entrusted the throne to the assembled lords, he had placed most of his trusted confidants in the Jiang Shi brothers.
translations.idiomatic: At first, though Gaozong had entrusted the throne to the chief ministers, he had placed his true confidants in the Jiang brothers.

sentences.zh: 二江更直殿內，動止關之。

translations.literal: The two Jiangs alternated duty inside the palace hall; all movements and stops were tied to them.
translations.idiomatic: The two Jiang brothers rotated duty in the inner palace; the emperor's every move depended on them.

sentences.zh: 帝稍欲行意，徐孝嗣不能奪，蕭坦之時有異同，而祏執制堅確，帝深忿之。

translations.literal: The emperor gradually wished to follow his own will; Xu Xiaosi could not override him, Xiao Tanzhi sometimes differed, but Shi held firm control—the emperor deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gradually wanted his own way; Xu Xiaosi could not check him, Xiao Tanzhi sometimes disagreed, but Jiang Shi held firm—and the emperor hated him for it.

sentences.zh: 帝左右會稽茹法珍、吳興梅蟲兒等，為帝所委任，祏常裁折之，法珍等切齒。

translations.literal: At the emperor's side were Rufazhen of Kuaiji, Meichong'er of Wuxing, and others, entrusted by the emperor; Shi often cut them down, and Fazhen and the rest gnashed their teeth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's favorites Rufazhen of Kuaiji and Meichong'er of Wuxing and others enjoyed his trust; Jiang Shi often rebuked them, and they hated him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 徐都嗣謂祏曰：「主上稍有異同，詎可盡相乖反！」

translations.literal: Director Xu said to Shi: "When the sovereign differs slightly, how can one oppose him on every point!"
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xiaosi told Jiang Shi, "When the emperor disagrees a little, must you oppose him on everything!"

sentences.zh: 祏曰：「但以見付，必無所憂。」

translations.literal: Shi said: "I was merely entrusted with the charge—there is surely nothing to worry about."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shi replied, "I was simply given the trust—I have nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 帝失德浸彰，祏議廢帝，立江夏王寶玄。

translations.literal: The emperor's loss of virtue grew ever plainer; Shi proposed deposing the emperor and raising Prince Bao Xuan of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor's misconduct became ever clearer, Jiang Shi proposed deposing him and enthroning Prince Bao Xuan of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 劉暄嘗為寶玄郢州行事，執事過刻。

translations.literal: Liu Xuan had once served as acting governor of Ying for Bao Xuan and was excessively harsh in office.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan had once acted as Ying governor for Bao Xuan and ruled with excessive severity.

sentences.zh: 有人獻馬，寶玄欲觀之，暄曰：「馬何用觀！」

translations.literal: Someone presented a horse; Bao Xuan wished to view it; Xuan said: "What use is there in viewing a horse!"
translations.idiomatic: When someone presented a horse, Bao Xuan wanted to see it; Xuan said, "What is there to see in a horse!"

sentences.zh: 妃索煮肫，帳下咨暄，暄曰：「旦已煮鵝，不煩復此。」

translations.literal: The consort asked for boiled gizzard; the staff consulted Xuan; Xuan said: "This morning goose was already boiled—no need to trouble with this again."
translations.idiomatic: When the princess consort asked for boiled gizzard, the staff consulted Xuan; he said, "We already boiled goose this morning—no need for this too."

sentences.zh: 寶玄恚曰：「舅殊無渭陽情。」

translations.literal: Bao Xuan angrily said: "My uncle utterly lacks the affection of Weiyang."
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xuan fumed, "My uncle has none of a mother's brother's kindness."

sentences.zh: 暄由是忌寶玄，不同祏議，更欲立建安王寶寅。

translations.literal: From this Xuan came to resent Bao Xuan, did not agree with Shi's proposal, and instead wished to raise Prince Bao Yin of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Xuan resented Bao Xuan, broke with Jiang Shi's plan, and wanted Prince Bao Yin of Jian'an instead.

sentences.zh: 祏密謀於始安王遙光，遙光自以年長，意欲自取，以微旨動祏。

translations.literal: Shi secretly plotted with Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an; Yaoguang, considering himself the elder, wished to take the throne himself and moved Shi with a subtle hint.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shi secretly plotted with Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an; Yaoguang, as the elder prince, wanted the throne for himself and dropped hints to Jiang Shi.

sentences.zh: 祏弟祀亦以少主難保，勸祏立遙光。

translations.literal: Shi's younger brother Si also thought the young sovereign hard to preserve and urged Shi to establish Yaoguang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Si too thought the young emperor could not be kept and urged his brother to put Yaoguang on the throne.

sentences.zh: 祏意回惑，以問蕭坦之。

translations.literal: Shi's mind wavered in confusion, and he asked Xiao Tanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shi wavered and consulted Xiao Tanzhi.

sentences.zh: 坦之時居母喪，起復為領軍將軍，謂祏曰：「明帝立，已非次，天下至今不服。

translations.literal: Tanzhi was then in mourning for his mother but had been recalled to serve as General-in-Chief of the Resolute Army; he said to Shi: "When Ming Di was enthroned, it was already out of turn—the realm to this day does not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhi was in mourning but had been recalled as General-in-Chief of the Resolute Army; he told Jiang Shi, "Ming Di's succession was already irregular—the realm never accepted it.

sentences.zh: 若復為此，恐四主瓦解，我期不敢言耳。」

translations.literal: If we do this again, I fear the four rulers will crumble and split—I dare not speak of what awaits us."
translations.idiomatic: Do this again and the dynasty may shatter—I dare not say what would become of us."

sentences.zh: 遂還宅行喪。

translations.literal: He then returned home to observe mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to resume mourning.

sentences.zh: 祏、祀密謂吏部郎謝朓曰：「江夏年少，脫不堪負荷，豈可復行廢立！

translations.literal: Shi and Si secretly said to Secretariat Director Xie Tiao: "Jiangxia is young; if he cannot bear the burden, how can we again carry out deposition and enthronement!
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shi and Jiang Si secretly told Directorate Director Xie Tiao, "Jiangxia is young and may not bear the weight—how can we depose and enthrone again!

sentences.zh: 始安年長，入纂不乖物望。

translations.literal: Shi'an is the elder; succeeding to the throne would not violate public expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Shi'an is older; his accession would meet with general approval.

sentences.zh: 非以此要富貴，政是求安國家耳。」

translations.literal: It is not that we seek wealth and rank by this—we simply wish to secure the state."
translations.idiomatic: We seek not fortune for ourselves but only the safety of the realm."

sentences.zh: 遙光又遣所親丹陽丞南陽劉祏密緻意於祏，欲引以為黨，祏不答。

translations.literal: Yaoguang again sent his intimate Liu Zhi of Nanyang, magistrate of Danyang, to convey his intimate wishes secretly to Shi, wishing to draw him into a faction; Shi did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoguang also sent his confidant Liu Zhi of Nanyang, magistrate of Danyang, to sound Jiang Shi out and draw him into a faction; Jiang Shi did not reply.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遙光以朓兼知衛尉事，朓懼，即以祏謀告太子右衛率左興盛，興盛不敢發。

translations.literal: Before long Yaoguang had Tiao additionally supervise the Commandant of the Guard; Tiao was afraid and reported Shi's plot to Left Xingsheng, Right Guard Leader of the Heir Apparent; Xingsheng dared not act.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yaoguang put Tiao in charge of the Commandant of the Guard as well; frightened, Tiao reported Jiang Shi's plot to Left Xingsheng, Right Guard Leader of the Heir Apparent—who dared not move.

sentences.zh: 朓又說劉暄曰：「始安一旦南面，則劉渢、劉晏居卿今地，但以卿為反覆人耳。」

translations.literal: Tiao again said to Liu Xuan: "Once Shi'an faces south as sovereign, Liu Hun and Liu Yan will occupy your present positions—you will merely be seen as a turncoat."
translations.idiomatic: Tiao also told Liu Xuan, "When Shi'an takes the throne, Liu Hun and Liu Yan will hold your posts—you will be treated as nothing but a turncoat."

sentences.zh: 晏者，遙光城局參軍也。

translations.literal: Yan was Yaoguang's garrison bureau officer.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was Yaoguang's city bureau officer.

sentences.zh: 暄陽驚，馳告遙光及祏。

translations.literal: Xuan feigned surprise and galloped to tell Yaoguang and Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan feigned shock and rode at once to warn Yaoguang and Jiang Shi.

sentences.zh: 遙光欲出朓為東陽郡，朓常輕祏，祏尉議除之。

translations.literal: Yaoguang wished to send Tiao out as prefect of Dongyang; Tiao often slighted Shi, and Shi counseled against removing him.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoguang wanted to send Tiao away as prefect of Dongyang; Tiao often slighted Jiang Shi, but Shi urged against dismissing him.

sentences.zh: 遙光乃收朓付廷尉，與孝嗣、祏、暄等連名啟「朓扇動內外，妄貶乘輿，竊論宮禁，間謗親賢，輕議朝宰。」

translations.literal: Yaoguang then seized Tiao and handed him to the Court of Judicial Review; together with Xiaosi, Shi, Xuan, and others he submitted a joint memorial: "Tiao has stirred inside and outside, wantonly belittled the imperial carriage, privately discussed palace prohibitions, slanderously spoken between of kin and worthies, and lightly critiqued court ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Yaoguang then arrested Tiao and handed him to the Court of Judicial Review; with Xiaosi, Jiang Shi, Xuan, and others he filed a joint memorial accusing Tiao of stirring court and country, slandering the throne, discussing palace affairs in secret, defaming kin and worthies, and slighting the ministers."

sentences.zh: 朓遂死獄中。

translations.literal: Tiao then died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Tiao died in prison.

sentences.zh: 暄以遙光若立，己失元舅之尊，不肯同祏議；

translations.literal: Xuan thought that if Yaoguang were enthroned he would lose the honor of chief maternal uncle and would not agree with Shi's proposal;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan feared that if Yaoguang took the throne he would lose his status as chief maternal uncle and refused to back Jiang Shi;

sentences.zh: 故祏遲疑久不決。

translations.literal: therefore Shi hesitated long and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: so Jiang Shi hesitated for a long time without deciding.

sentences.zh: 遙光大怒，遣左右黃曇慶刺暄於青溪橋。

translations.literal: Yaoguang was greatly angered and sent his attendant Huang Tanqing to assassinate Xuan at Qingxi Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoguang was furious and sent his attendant Huang Tanqing to kill Xuan at Qingxi Bridge.

sentences.zh: 曇慶見暄部伍多，不敢發；

translations.literal: Tanqing saw that Xuan's escort was large and dared not strike;
translations.idiomatic: Tanqing saw Xuan's large escort and did not dare act;

sentences.zh: 暄覺之，遂發祏謀，帝命收祏兄弟。

translations.literal: Xuan perceived this and thereupon exposed Shi's plot; the emperor ordered the arrest of the Jiang brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan caught on and exposed Jiang Shi's plot; the emperor ordered the Jiang brothers seized.

sentences.zh: 時祀直內殿，疑有異，遣信報祏曰：「劉暄似有異謀。

translations.literal: At that time Si was on duty in the inner hall; suspecting something amiss, he sent a messenger to report to Shi: "Liu Xuan seems to have some unusual plot.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Si was on duty in the inner palace; sensing trouble, he sent word to Jiang Shi: "Liu Xuan seems to be up to something.

sentences.zh: 今作何計？」

translations.literal: What plan shall we make now?"
translations.idiomatic: What shall we do now?"

sentences.zh: 祏曰：「政當靜以鎮之。」

translations.literal: Shi said: "We should just meet it with calm to suppress it."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shi said, "We need only stay calm."

sentences.zh: 俄有詔召祏入見，停中書省。

translations.literal: Shortly an edict summoned Shi to audience; he was detained at the Secretariat Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict summoned Jiang Shi to court; he was held at the Secretariat Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 初，袁文曠以斬王敬則功當封，祏執不與；

translations.literal: Earlier, Yuan Wenkuan for the merit of beheading Wang Jingze deserved enfeoffment; Shi insisted on not granting it;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yuan Wenkuan had earned a fief for killing Wang Jingze, but Jiang Shi blocked it;

sentences.zh: 帝使文曠取祏，文曠以刀環築其心曰：「復能奪我封不！」

translations.literal: the emperor had Wenkuan seize Shi; Wenkuan struck Shi's heart with a sword pommel and said: "Can you again steal my fief or not!"
translations.idiomatic: the emperor had Wenkuan seize Jiang Shi; Wenkuan rammed the pommel of his sword into Shi's chest and shouted, "Can you steal my fief now!"

sentences.zh: 並弟祀皆死。

translations.literal: He and his younger brother Si both died.
translations.idiomatic: Both he and his brother Si were killed.

sentences.zh: 劉暄聞祏等死，眠中大驚，投出戶外，問左右：「收至未？」

translations.literal: Liu Xuan heard that Shi and the others were dead; startled in his sleep he threw himself outside the door and asked those at hand: "Have they come to seize me yet?"
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xuan heard the Jiang brothers were dead, he bolted upright in sleep and fell out the door, asking his attendants, "Have they come for me yet?"

sentences.zh: 良久，意定，還坐，大悲曰：「不念江，行自痛也！」

translations.literal: After a long while his mind settled; he returned and sat down and said in great grief: "Not thinking of Jiang—I will soon be pained myself!"
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he calmed down, sat again, and wailed, "I gave no thought to Jiang—and now I will pay for it myself!"

sentences.zh: 帝自是無所忌憚，益得自恣，日夜與近習於後堂鼓叫戲馬。

translations.literal: From this the emperor had nothing to fear or restrain him and indulged himself all the more, day and night with his intimates in the rear hall drumming, shouting, and racing horses in sport.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the emperor feared nothing and indulged himself freely, day and night drumming, shouting, and racing horses in the rear hall with his favorites.

sentences.zh: 常以五更就寢，至晡乃起。

translations.literal: He regularly went to bed at the fifth watch and rose only at the hour of shen (late afternoon).
translations.idiomatic: He usually slept from the fifth watch until late afternoon.

sentences.zh: 群臣節、朔朝見，晡後方前，或際暗遣出。

translations.literal: When ministers attended on festival and new-moon days, they were only admitted after shen; sometimes at the edge of dark they were sent out.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers attending court on festival and new-moon days were not admitted until afternoon; sometimes they were dismissed at dusk.

sentences.zh: 台閣案奏，月數十日乃報，或不知所在；

translations.literal: Memorials from the offices took a month or ten days to receive reply, or their whereabouts were unknown;
