translations.idiomatic: Memorials from the bureaus might go unanswered for weeks, or vanish entirely;

sentences.zh: 宦者以裹魚肉還家，並是五省黃案。

translations.literal: eunuchs wrapped fish and meat to take home—all of it yellow-sealed dossiers from the five ministries.
translations.idiomatic: eunuchs carried fish and meat home wrapped in yellow-sealed documents from the five ministries.

sentences.zh: 帝常習騎致適，顧謂左右曰：「江祏常禁吾乘馬；

translations.literal: The emperor often practiced riding to his pleasure and turning to those at hand said: "Jiang Shi always forbade my riding horses;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often rode for pleasure and told his attendants, "Jiang Shi always stopped me from riding;

sentences.zh: 小子若在，吾豈能得此！」

translations.literal: if that stripling were still alive, how could I have gotten this!"
translations.idiomatic: if that wretch were still alive, could I enjoy this!"

sentences.zh: 因問：「祏親戚餘誰？」

translations.literal: He then asked: "Who among Shi's kin still remains?"
translations.idiomatic: He then asked, "Who is left among Jiang Shi's kin?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「江祥今在冶。」

translations.literal: They answered: "Jiang Xiang is now at the prison works."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "Jiang Xiang is at the prison works."

sentences.zh: 帝於馬上作敕，賜祥死。

translations.literal: The emperor from horseback drafted an edict and granted Xiang death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor drafted an edict on horseback and had Xiang executed.

sentences.zh: 始安王遙光素有異志，與其弟荊州刺史遙欣密謀舉兵據東府，使遙欣自江陵引兵急下，刻期將發，而遙欣病卒。

translations.literal: Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an had long had divergent ambitions; with his younger brother Yaoxin, governor of Jing Province, he secretly plotted to raise troops and hold the Eastern Quarter, having Yaoxin lead troops hastily down from Jiangling on a fixed date—they were about to move when Yaoxin died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an had long harbored ambitions; with his brother Yaoxin, governor of Jing, he secretly planned to raise troops and seize the Eastern Quarter, with Yaoxin rushing down from Jiangling on a set date—but Yaoxin died before they could move.

sentences.zh: 江祏被誅，帝召遙光入殿，告以祏罪，遙光懼，還省，即陽狂號哭，遂稱疾不復入台。

translations.literal: When Jiang Shi was executed the emperor summoned Yaoguang into the hall and told him of Shi's crimes; Yaoguang was afraid; returning to his quarters he at once feigned madness and wailed, then claimed illness and no longer entered the capital offices.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiang Shi was executed the emperor summoned Yaoguang and told him of Shi's crimes; terrified, Yaoguang went home, feigned madness and wailed, then pleaded illness and stopped coming to court.

sentences.zh: 先是，遙光弟豫州刺史遙昌卒，其部曲皆歸遙光。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yaoguang's younger brother Yaochang, governor of Yu Province, had died, and his troops all passed to Yaoguang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yaoguang's brother Yaochang, governor of Yu, had died, and his troops had passed to Yaoguang.

sentences.zh: 及遙欣喪還，停東府前渚，荊州眾力送者甚盛。

translations.literal: When Yaoxin's coffin returned it halted at the ford before the Eastern Quarter; the Jingzhou escort was very grand.
translations.idiomatic: When Yaoxin's funeral cortege returned it stopped at the landing before the Eastern Quarter, with a massive escort from Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 帝既誅二江，慮遙光不自安，欲遷為司徒，使還第，召入諭旨。

translations.literal: The emperor having executed the two Jiangs, fearing Yaoguang would not feel secure, wished to transfer him to Grand Steward and have him return to his residence; he summoned him in to explain his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Having killed the two Jiangs, the emperor feared Yaoguang's unease and planned to make him Grand Steward and send him home; he summoned him to explain.

sentences.zh: 遙光恐見殺，乙卯晡時，收集二州部曲於東府東門，召劉渢、劉晏等謀舉兵，以討劉暄為名。

translations.literal: Yaoguang feared he would be killed; at the hour of shen on yimao he gathered the troops of the two provinces at the east gate of the Eastern Quarter, summoned Liu Hun, Liu Yan, and others to plot raising troops, under the banner of punishing Liu Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing execution, at late afternoon on yimao Yaoguang assembled troops from both provinces at the Eastern Quarter's east gate, called Liu Hun, Liu Yan, and others to raise arms in the name of punishing Liu Xuan.

sentences.zh: 夜，遣數百人破東冶，出囚，於尚方取仗。

translations.literal: At night he sent several hundred men to break into the Eastern Prison Works, release prisoners, and take weapons from the Imperial Workshop.
translations.idiomatic: That night he sent hundreds of men to smash the Eastern Prison Works, free prisoners, and seize arms from the Imperial Workshop.

sentences.zh: 又召驍騎將軍垣歷生，歷生隨信而至。

translations.literal: He also summoned Fierce Cavalry General Yuan Lisheng; Lisheng came as soon as the message arrived.
translations.idiomatic: He also summoned Fierce Cavalry General Yuan Lisheng, who came at once.

sentences.zh: 蕭坦之宅在東府城東，遙光遣人掩取之，坦之露袒逾牆走向台。

translations.literal: Xiao Tanzhi's residence was east of the Eastern Quarter city; Yaoguang sent men to seize him by surprise; Tanzhi bared his torso, climbed over the wall, and fled toward the capital offices.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Tanzhi lived east of the Eastern Quarter; Yaoguang sent men to seize him; Tanzhi stripped to the waist, climbed the wall, and fled toward the palace offices.

sentences.zh: 道逢游邏主顏端，執之，坦之告以遙光反，不信；

translations.literal: On the road he met patrol chief Yan Duan, who seized him; Tanzhi told him of Yaoguang's rebellion, but Duan did not believe;
translations.idiomatic: On the way he met patrol chief Yan Duan, who detained him; Tanzhi told him Yaoguang had rebelled, but Duan did not believe him;

sentences.zh: 自往詷問，知實，乃以馬與坦之，相隨入台。

translations.literal: he himself went to inquire and learned it was true; he then gave Tanzhi a horse and entered the offices together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Duan went to investigate himself, found it true, gave Tanzhi a horse, and entered the palace with him.

sentences.zh: 遙光又掩取尚書左僕射沈文季於其宅，欲以為都督，會文季已入台。

translations.literal: Yaoguang again sent men to seize Left Vice Minister Shen Wenji at his residence, wishing to make him commander-in-chief, but Wenji had already entered the offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoguang also tried to seize Left Vice Minister Shen Wenji at home to make him commander-in-chief, but Wenji was already at court.

sentences.zh: 垣歷生說遙光帥城內兵夜攻台，輦荻燒城門，曰：「公但乘輿隨後，反掌可克！」

translations.literal: Yuan Lisheng urged Yaoguang to lead the troops within the city to attack the offices by night, haul reeds to burn the city gates, and said: "My lord need only ride in your carriage and follow after—in the turn of a palm it can be taken!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Lisheng urged Yaoguang to lead the garrison in a night assault on the palace, haul reeds to burn the gates, and said, "My lord need only follow in your carriage—you can take it in an instant!"

sentences.zh: 遙光狐疑不敢出。

translations.literal: Yaoguang wavered in doubt and dared not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoguang hesitated and would not move.

sentences.zh: 天稍曉，遙光戎服出聽事，命上仗登城行賞賜。

translations.literal: When the sky was slightly light Yaoguang in martial dress came out to the audience hall, ordered arms taken up, mounted the wall, and distributed rewards.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Yaoguang appeared in armor at headquarters, ordered troops armed and onto the walls, and distributed rewards.

sentences.zh: 歷生復勸出軍，遙光不肯，冀台中自有變。

translations.literal: Lisheng again urged him to lead the army out; Yaoguang refused, hoping the offices themselves would produce a change.
translations.idiomatic: Lisheng again urged him to march out; Yaoguang refused, hoping the palace would collapse on its own.

sentences.zh: 及日出，台軍稍至。

translations.literal: When the sun rose the capital garrison gradually arrived.
translations.idiomatic: As the sun rose palace troops began to arrive.

sentences.zh: 台中始聞亂，眾情惶惑；

translations.literal: The offices had only just heard of the disturbance; men's minds were alarmed and confused;
translations.idiomatic: The palace had only just learned of the revolt and panic spread;

sentences.zh: 向曉，有詔召徐孝嗣，孝嗣入，人心乃安。

translations.literal: toward dawn an edict summoned Xu Xiaosi; when Xiaosi entered, men's hearts then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Near dawn an edict summoned Xu Xiaosi; when he arrived, order was restored.

sentences.zh: 左將軍沈聞變，馳入西掖門。

translations.literal: Left General Shen heard of the upheaval and galloped in through the Western Side Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Left General Shen heard of the revolt and raced in through the Western Side Gate.

sentences.zh: 或勸戎服，約曰：「台中方擾攘，見我戎服，或者謂同遙光。」

translations.literal: Someone urged him to wear martial dress; he said approximately: "The offices are in turmoil just now—if they see me in martial dress, some may think I am with Yaoguang."
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to wear armor; he said roughly, "The palace is in chaos—if they see me armed, some may think I side with Yaoguang."

sentences.zh: 乃朱衣而入。

translations.literal: He then entered in vermillion robes.
translations.idiomatic: He entered in court dress instead.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，詔曲赦建康，中外戒嚴。

translations.literal: On bingchen an edict ordered a partial amnesty for Jiankang and martial law within and without.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen the court declared a partial amnesty for Jiankang and put the capital under martial law.

sentences.zh: 徐孝嗣以下屯衛宮城，蕭坦之帥台軍討遙光。

translations.literal: Xu Xiaosi and those below garrisoned and guarded the palace city; Xiao Tanzhi led the capital garrison to attack Yaoguang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xiaosi and others garrisoned the palace; Xiao Tanzhi led palace troops against Yaoguang.

sentences.zh: 孝嗣內自疑懼，與沈文季戎服共坐南掖門上，欲與之共論世事，文季輒引以他辭，終不得及。

translations.literal: Xiaosi inwardly doubted and feared; in martial dress he sat together with Shen Wenji atop the Southern Side Gate, wishing to discuss affairs of the age with him; Wenji always diverted the talk to other subjects and in the end never reached it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosi was inwardly afraid; in armor he sat with Shen Wenji atop the Southern Side Gate hoping to discuss the situation, but Wenji kept changing the subject and never would.

sentences.zh: 蕭坦之屯湘宮寺，左興盛屯東籬門，鎮軍司馬曹虎屯青溪大橋。

translations.literal: Xiao Tanzhi encamped at Xianggong Temple; Left Xingsheng encamped at the Eastern Hedge Gate; Pacifying Army Major Cao Hu encamped at Great Qingxi Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Tanzhi encamped at Xianggong Temple, Left Xingsheng at the Eastern Hedge Gate, and Pacifying Army Major Cao Hu at Great Qingxi Bridge.

sentences.zh: 眾軍圍東城三面，燒司徒府。

translations.literal: The combined armies besieged the eastern city on three sides and burned the Grand Steward's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: The armies surrounded the eastern city on three sides and burned the Grand Steward's residence.

sentences.zh: 遙光遣垣歷生從西門出戰，台軍屢敗，殺軍主桑天愛。

translations.literal: Yaoguang sent Yuan Lisheng out through the west gate to fight; the capital garrison was repeatedly defeated and lost its commander Sang Tian'ai.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoguang sent Yuan Lisheng out the west gate; palace troops were repeatedly beaten and lost their commander Sang Tian'ai.

sentences.zh: 遙光之起兵也，問咨議參軍蕭暢，暢正色不從。

translations.literal: When Yaoguang raised troops he questioned Consultant Officer Xiao Chang; Chang with stern countenance refused to follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Yaoguang rebelled he asked consultant officer Xiao Chang, who refused with a stern face.

sentences.zh: 戊午，暢與撫軍長史沈昭略潛自南門出，詣台自歸，眾情大沮。

translations.literal: On wuwu Chang and Pacifying Army Chief Clerk Shen Zhaolue secretly went out from the south gate, came to the offices and surrendered themselves—the morale of the host was greatly crushed.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Chang and Pacifying Army chief clerk Shen Zhaolue slipped out the south gate and surrendered at court; Yaoguang's followers lost heart.

sentences.zh: 暢，衍之弟；

translations.literal: Chang was Yan's younger brother;
translations.idiomatic: Chang was Xiao Yan's younger brother;

sentences.zh: 昭略，文季之兄子也。

translations.literal: Zhaolue was Wenji's elder brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolue was Shen Wenji's nephew.

sentences.zh: 己未，垣歷生從南門出戰，因棄槊降曹虎，虎命斬之。

translations.literal: On jiwei Yuan Lisheng went out through the south gate to fight, then cast aside his spear and surrendered to Cao Hu; Hu ordered him beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Yuan Lisheng sallied from the south gate, then threw down his spear and surrendered to Cao Hu, who had him executed.

sentences.zh: 遙光大怒，於床上自踴，使殺歷生子。

translations.literal: Yaoguang was greatly enraged; on his bed he stomped himself and ordered Lisheng's sons killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoguang was furious; he stamped on his bed and ordered Lisheng's sons killed.

sentences.zh: 其晚，台軍以火箭燒東北角樓。

translations.literal: That evening the capital garrison used fire arrows to burn the northeast corner tower.
translations.idiomatic: That evening palace troops burned the northeast corner tower with fire arrows.

sentences.zh: 至夜，城潰，遙光還小齋帳中，著衣帢坐，秉燭自照，令人反拒，齋閣皆重關，左右並逾屋散出。

translations.literal: By night the city wall collapsed. Yaoguang returned to his small study tent, dressed in a headcloth cap and seated, holding a candle to illuminate himself; he had men bar the doors from within; the study chambers were all heavily barred, and his attendants all fled over the walls and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: When night fell the wall gave way. Yaoguang retreated to his small study, wearing a headcloth and sitting by candlelight. He had the doors barred from within and locked every door in the pavilion; his attendants all climbed over the walls and fled.

sentences.zh: 台軍主劉國寶等先入，遙光聞外兵至，滅燭扶匐床下。

translations.literal: The garrison commander Liu Guobao and others entered first; Yaoguang heard outside troops arriving, extinguished the candle, and crawled prostrate under the bed.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison commander Liu Guobao and his men were first to enter. Hearing troops outside, Yaoguang snuffed the candle and crawled under the bed.

sentences.zh: 軍人排閣入，於暗中牽出，斬之。

translations.literal: Soldiers forced through the pavilion and entered; in the darkness they dragged him out and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers broke into the pavilion, dragged him out in the dark, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 台軍入城，焚燒室屋且盡。

translations.literal: The capital garrison entered the city and burned nearly all the buildings and houses.
translations.idiomatic: Palace troops entered the city and burned nearly every building to the ground.

sentences.zh: 劉渢走還家，為人所殺。

translations.literal: Liu Huan fled home and was killed by someone.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huan fled to his home but was killed by his pursuers.

sentences.zh: 荊州將潘紹聞遙光作亂，謀欲應之。

translations.literal: The Jing Province general Pan Shao heard that Yaoguang had risen in rebellion and planned to respond to him.
translations.idiomatic: When General Pan Shao of Jing Province heard that Yaoguang had rebelled, he plotted to join him.

sentences.zh: 西部郎司馬夏侯詳呼紹議事，因斬之，州府以安。

translations.literal: The Western Department attendant's Major Xiahou Xiang summoned Shao to discuss affairs and thereupon beheaded him; the province and prefecture were thus pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Xiang, major to the Western Department attendant, summoned Shao on pretense of business and cut him down; the province and capital were thereby secured.

sentences.zh: 己巳，以徐孝嗣為司空；

translations.literal: On jisi Xu Xiaosi was made Minister of Works;
translations.idiomatic: On jisi Xu Xiaosi was appointed Minister of Works;

sentences.zh: 加沈文季鎮軍將軍，侍中、僕射如故；

translations.literal: Shen Wenji was given the additional post of General Who Pacifies the Army; he retained his titles as Palace Attendant and Vice Minister;
translations.idiomatic: Shen Wenji was made General Who Pacifies the Army while retaining his posts as Palace Attendant and Vice Minister;

sentences.zh: 蕭坦之為尚書右僕射、丹陽尹，右將軍如故；

translations.literal: Xiao Tanzhi was made Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Governor of Danyang; he retained his title as Right General;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Tanzhi was appointed Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Governor of Danyang, keeping his rank as Right General;

sentences.zh: 劉暄為領軍將軍；

translations.literal: Liu Xuan was made General of the Guards;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan was made General of the Guards;

sentences.zh: 曹虎為散騎常侍、右衛將軍。

translations.literal: Cao Hu was made Regular Attendant in Dispensation and Right Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Hu was appointed Regular Attendant in Dispensation and Right Guard General.

sentences.zh: 皆賞平始安之功也。

translations.literal: All these appointments were rewards for pacifying Shi'an.
translations.idiomatic: These were all rewards for putting down the rebellion at Shi'an.

sentences.zh: 魏南徐州刺史沈陵來降。

translations.literal: Shen Ling, governor of Southern Xu Province for Wei, came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Ling, Wei governor of Southern Xu Province, defected to Qi.

sentences.zh: 陵，文季之族子也。

translations.literal: Ling was a clansman of Wenji's.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Ling was a kinsman of Shen Wenji.

sentences.zh: 時魏徐州刺史京兆王愉年少，軍府事皆決於兼長史盧淵。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Yu of Jingzhao, governor of Xu Province for Wei, was young; all military headquarters affairs were decided by the acting Chief Administrator Lu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yu of Jingzhao, the young Wei governor of Xu Province, left all military affairs to his acting chief administrator Lu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 淵知陵將叛，敕諸城潛為之備；

translations.literal: Yuan knew that Ling was about to rebel and ordered the various garrisons to prepare secretly for it;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuan knew Shen Ling was about to rebel and quietly ordered the garrison towns to prepare;

sentences.zh: 屢以聞於魏朝，魏朝不聽。

translations.literal: He repeatedly reported this to the Wei court, but the Wei court would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He reported this to the Wei court repeatedly, but the court paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 陵遂殺將佐，帥宿預之眾來奔，濱淮諸戊以有備得全。

translations.literal: Ling thereupon killed his commanders and lieutenants, led the troops at Suyu to come and surrender; the various garrisons along the Huai were preserved because of the prior preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Ling then killed his officers, led the garrison at Suyu over to Qi, and the Huai river forts were saved thanks to Lu Yuan's preparations.

sentences.zh: 陵在邊歷年，陰結邊州豪傑。

translations.literal: Ling had been on the frontier for many years and had secretly allied with powerful families of the border provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Ling had spent years on the frontier cultivating ties with borderland magnates.

sentences.zh: 陵既叛，郡縣多捕送陵黨，淵皆撫而赦之，唯歸罪於陵，眾心乃安。

translations.literal: After Ling had rebelled, the commanderies and counties mostly captured and sent in his partisans; Yuan comforted and pardoned them all, laying blame on Ling alone, and popular sentiment was thereby calmed.
translations.idiomatic: After the defection, local authorities sent up many of Shen Ling's associates; Lu Yuan pardoned them one and all, pinning the guilt solely on Shen Ling, and the people were reassured.

sentences.zh: 閏月，丙子，立東陵公寶覽為始安王，奉靖王后。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on bingzi, Duke Baolan of Dongling was established as Prince of Shi'an to succeed Prince Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on bingzi, Duke Baolan of Dongling was made Prince of Shi'an to carry on the line of Prince Jing.

sentences.zh: 以沈陵為北徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Shen Ling was made governor of Northern Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Ling was appointed governor of Northern Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 江祏等既敗，帝左右捉刀、應敕之徒皆恣橫用事，時人謂之「刀敕」。

translations.literal: After Jiang Shi and the others had been defeated, the Emperor's attendants who carried swords and responded to edicts all acted with unrestrained violence in wielding power; people of the time called them the "Sword and Edict."
translations.idiomatic: After Jiang Shi and his faction fell, the emperor's sword-bearing attendants and edict-handlers ruled with impunity; contemporaries called them the "Blade Edicts."

sentences.zh: 蕭坦之剛很而專，嬖倖畏而憎之；

translations.literal: Xiao Tanzhi was stubborn, harsh, and domineering; the favored minions feared and hated him;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Tanzhi was headstrong and overbearing; the emperor's favorites both feared and resented him;

sentences.zh: 遙光死二十餘日，帝遣延明主帥黃齊濟將兵圍坦之宅，殺之，並其子秘書郎賞。

translations.literal: More than twenty days after Yaoguang's death, the Emperor sent Yanming chief commander Huang Qiji to lead troops to surround Tanzhi's residence and kill him, together with his son Shang, a secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: A little over twenty days after Yaoguang's death, the emperor sent chief commander Huang Qiji of Yanming with troops to surround Xiao Tanzhi's house. Tanzhi was killed, along with his son Shang, a secretary of the palace library.

sentences.zh: 坦之從兄翼宗為海陵太守，未發，坦之謂文濟曰：「從兄海陵宅故應無它。」

translations.literal: Tanzhi's elder clansman brother Yizong was governor of Hailing and had not yet departed; Tanzhi said to Wenji: "My elder clansman the governor of Hailing — his household ought to have nothing amiss."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Tanzhi's elder cousin Yizong had been appointed governor of Hailing but had not yet set out. Tanzhi told Wenji, "My cousin the governor of Hailing — surely nothing is amiss at his house."

sentences.zh: 文濟曰：「海陵宅在何處？」

translations.literal: Wenji said: "Where is the Hailing residence?"
translations.idiomatic: Where is the Hailing residence?" Wenji asked.

sentences.zh: 坦之以告。

translations.literal: Tanzhi told him.
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhi told him.

sentences.zh: 文濟白帝，帝仍遣收之。

translations.literal: Wenji reported to the Emperor, and the Emperor again sent men to seize Yizong.
translations.idiomatic: Wenji reported to the emperor, who sent men to arrest Yizong as well.

sentences.zh: 檢其家，至貧，唯有質錢貼數百，還以啟帝，原其死，系尚方。

translations.literal: Searching his household, they found extreme poverty — only several hundred pawn tickets; this was reported back to the Emperor, who spared his life and imprisoned him in the Palace Workshop.
translations.idiomatic: A search of his home turned up only a few hundred pawn tickets — he was utterly destitute. The emperor spared his life and sent him to the Palace Workshop as a prisoner.

sentences.zh: 茹法珍等譖劉暄有異志，帝曰：「暄是我舅，豈應有此？」

translations.literal: Ru Fazhen and others slandered Liu Xuan as having different intentions; the Emperor said: "Xuan is my mother's brother — how could he have such intentions?"
translations.idiomatic: Ru Fazhen and others accused Liu Xuan of disloyalty. The emperor said, "Xuan is my uncle — he wouldn't do such a thing, would he?

sentences.zh: 直閣新蔡徐世標曰：「明帝乃武帝同堂，恩遇如此，猶滅武帝之後；

translations.literal: Palace attendant of Xincai Xu Shibiao said: "Emperor Ming was Emperor Wu's paternal cousin and received such grace and favor, yet he still extinguished Emperor Wu's descendants;
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant Xu Shibiao of Xincai said, "Emperor Ming was Emperor Wu's own cousin, and look how well the court treated him — yet he still wiped out Emperor Wu's line.

sentences.zh: 舅焉可信邪！」

translations.literal: How can a maternal uncle be trusted!"
translations.idiomatic: What makes you think you can trust an uncle!

sentences.zh: 遂殺之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan was put to death.

sentences.zh: 曹虎善於誘納，日食荒客常數百人。

translations.literal: Cao Hu was skilled at inviting and receiving men; every day he fed several hundred vagabond guests.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Hu was a generous host who daily entertained several hundred penniless guests at his table.

sentences.zh: 晚節吝嗇，罷雍州，有錢五千萬，它物稱是。

translations.literal: In his later years he became stingy; when removed from Yong Province he had fifty million in cash, with other goods to match.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he turned miserly; when he left his post as governor of Yong Province he had fifty million in cash and commensurate possessions besides.

sentences.zh: 帝疑虎舊將，且利其財，遂殺之。

translations.literal: The Emperor suspected Hu as an old general and coveted his wealth, and so had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor distrusted him as a veteran general and coveted his fortune, and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 坦之、暄、虎所新除官，皆未及拜而死。

translations.literal: The newly conferred posts of Tanzhi, Xuan, and Hu — none had yet been formally assumed before they died.
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhi, Xuan, and Hu were all killed before they could even assume their newly granted offices.

sentences.zh: 初，高宗臨殂，以降昌事戒帝曰：「作事不可在人後。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Gaozong was on his deathbed, he warned the Emperor with the affair of Jiang Chang, saying: "In acting, one must not be behind others."
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Emperor Gaozong had warned the emperor, citing the Jiang Chang affair: "When you act, do not let others get ahead of you.

sentences.zh: 故帝數與近習謀誅大臣，皆發於倉猝，決意無疑。

translations.literal: Therefore the Emperor often plotted with close attendants to execute great ministers; all such moves erupted in sudden haste, with resolve and no hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the emperor often conspired with his intimates to kill high ministers, always striking suddenly and without second thoughts.

sentences.zh: 於是大臣人人莫能自保。

translations.literal: Thereupon not one of the great ministers could protect himself.
translations.idiomatic: No senior official could feel safe.

sentences.zh: 九月，丁未，以豫州刺史裴叔業為南兗州刺史，征虜長史張沖為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on dingwei, Governor Pei Shuye of Yu Province was made governor of Southern Yan Province; Chief Administrator Zhang Chong of the General Who Campaigns against Barbarians was made governor of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on dingwei, Pei Shuye was transferred from Yu Province to Southern Yan Province, and Zhang Chong, chief administrator to the campaigning general, was made governor of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以頻誅大臣，大赦。

translations.literal: On renxu, because ministers had been frequently executed, a general amnesty was declared.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu a general amnesty was proclaimed after the spate of ministerial executions.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，魏主謁長陵，欲引白衣左右吳人茹皓同車。

translations.literal: On bingxu the Wei emperor visited Changling and wished to have the commoner attendant Wu native Ru Hao ride in the same carriage.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu the Wei emperor paid homage at Changling and wanted his commoner attendant Ru Hao, a man of Wu, to share his carriage.

sentences.zh: 皓奮衣將登，給事黃門侍郎無匡進諫，帝推之使下，皓失色而退。

translations.literal: Hao eagerly adjusted his clothes and was about to mount; Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate Attendant Wu Kuang remonstrated; the Emperor pushed him aside to get down; Hao turned pale and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Ru Hao was about to climb aboard when Supervising Secretary Yuan Kuang of the Yellow Gate remonstrated. The emperor pushed Kuang aside; Ru Hao blanched and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 匡，新城之子也。

translations.literal: Kuang was the son of Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Kuang was the son of Yuan Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史劉季連聞帝失德，遂自驕恣，用刑嚴酷，蜀人怨之。

translations.literal: Governor Liu Jilian of Yi Province heard that the Emperor was devoid of virtue and thereupon became arrogant and unrestrained himself, applying punishments with harsh severity; the people of Shu resented him.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor Liu Jilian of Yi Province heard of the emperor's depravity, he grew arrogant and cruel in his own rule; the people of Shu bitterly resented him.

sentences.zh: 是月，遣兵襲中水，不克。

translations.literal: That month he sent troops to attack Zhongshui but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: That month he sent troops against Zhongshui but failed to take it.

sentences.zh: 於是蜀人趙續伯等皆起兵作亂，季連不能制。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Shu men Zhao Xubo and others all raised troops in rebellion; Jilian could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xubo and other Shu men then rose in revolt, and Jilian could not suppress them.

sentences.zh: 枝江文忠公徐孝嗣，以文士不顯同異，故名位雖重，猶得久存。

translations.literal: Duke Wenzhong of Zhijiang, Xu Xiaosi, because as a literary man he did not manifest taking sides, though his fame and rank were weighty, still managed to survive long.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xiaosi, Duke Wenzhong of Zhijiang, stayed unobtrusive as a scholar-official who never openly picked sides; despite his eminence he managed to survive longer than others.

sentences.zh: 虎賁中郎將許准為孝嗣陳說事機，勸行廢立。

translations.literal: Tiger Guard Commandant Xu Zhun explained the situation to Xiaosi and urged him to carry out deposition and enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhun, a commandant of the Tiger Guards, laid out the situation to Xu Xiaosi and urged him to depose the emperor and install a replacement.

sentences.zh: 孝嗣遲疑久之，謂必無用干戈之理；

translations.literal: Xiaosi hesitated for a long time, saying there surely was no reason to use arms;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xiaosi wavered for a long time, insisting there was no need for force of arms;

sentences.zh: 須帝出遊，閉城門，召百僚集議廢之。

translations.literal: one must wait until the Emperor goes out on tour, close the city gates, summon the hundred officials to assemble and deliberate on deposing him.
translations.idiomatic: they need only wait until the emperor went out on an excursion, then shut the gates, summon the officials, and vote to remove him.

sentences.zh: 雖有此懷，終不能決。

translations.literal: Though he harbored such intent, in the end he could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: He entertained such plans but could never bring himself to act.

sentences.zh: 諸嬖倖亦稍憎之。

translations.literal: The various favored minions also gradually came to dislike him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's favorites gradually turned against him as well.

sentences.zh: 西豐忠憲侯沈文季自托老疾，不豫朝權，侍中沈昭略謂文季曰：「叔父行年六十，為員外僕射，欲求自免，豈可得乎！」

translations.literal: Marquis Zhongxian of Xifeng, Shen Wenji, pleading old age and illness, did not participate in court power; Palace Attendant Shen Zhaolue said to Wenji: "Uncle, at sixty years of age serving as an extraordinary Vice Minister — if you wish to save yourself, how can that be possible!"
translations.idiomatic: Shen Wenji, Marquis Zhongxian of Xifeng, had withdrawn on pretext of age and illness, staying out of court politics. His nephew Shen Zhaolue, a palace attendant, told him, "Uncle, you are sixty and still serving as extraordinary vice minister — do you really think you can escape unscathed?

sentences.zh: 文季笑而不應。

translations.literal: Wenji smiled and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Wenji smiled and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，乙未，帝召孝嗣、文季、昭略入華林省。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on yimei, the Emperor summoned Xiaosi, Wenji, and Zhaolue into Hualin Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on yimei, the emperor summoned Xu Xiaosi, Shen Wenji, and Shen Zhaolue to Hualin Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 文季登車，顧曰：「此行恐往而不反。」

translations.literal: Wenji mounted his carriage and looking back said: "This journey — I fear I shall go but not return."
translations.idiomatic: As Shen Wenji boarded his carriage he looked back and said, "I doubt I shall return from this."

sentences.zh: 帝使外監茹法珍賜以藥酒，昭略怒，罵孝嗣曰：「廢昏立明，古今令典；

translations.literal: The Emperor had Outer Intendant Ru Fazhen bestow poisoned wine; Zhaolue was angry and cursed Xiaosi, saying: "Deposing the benighted and establishing the enlightened is the fine norm of ancient and modern times;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Outer Intendant Ru Fazhen present them with poisoned wine. Shen Zhaolue flew into a rage and cursed Xu Xiaosi: "Deposing a dark ruler and raising a wise one is the timeless duty of a minister;

sentences.zh: 宰相無才，致有今日！」

translations.literal: a chief minister without talent brings about today!"
translations.idiomatic: yet a chancellor without courage has brought us to this pass!"

sentences.zh: 以甌擲其面曰：「使作破面鬼！」

translations.literal: He threw a bowl at his face, saying: "Go be a face-smashing ghost!"
translations.idiomatic: He hurled a bowl at Xu Xiaosi's face, crying, "May you go a ghost with a broken face!"

sentences.zh: 孝嗣飲藥酒至斗餘，乃卒。

translations.literal: Xiaosi drank the poisoned wine to more than a dou before he died.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xiaosi drank more than a dou of the poisoned wine before he died.

sentences.zh: 孝嗣子演尚武康公主，況尚山陰公主，皆坐誅。

translations.literal: Xiaosi's sons Yan, who had married Princess Wukang, and Kuang, who had married Princess Shanyin, were both executed by association.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Yan, husband of Princess Wukang, and Kuang, husband of Princess Shanyin, were executed as well.

sentences.zh: 昭略弟昭光聞收至，家人勸之逃。

translations.literal: Zhaolue's younger brother Zhaoguang heard that arrest was coming; his family urged him to flee.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Zhaoguang, Zhaolue's younger brother, learned that arrest was imminent, his family urged him to flee.

sentences.zh: 昭光不忍捨其母，入，執母手悲泣，收者殺之。

translations.literal: Zhaoguang could not bear to abandon his mother; he entered, took his mother's hand and wept in grief; the arresters killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He could not bear to leave his mother, went in to clasp her hand and weep — and the arresters killed him there.

sentences.zh: 昭光兄子曇亮逃，已得免，聞昭光死，歎曰：「家門屠滅，何以生為！」

translations.literal: Zhaoguang's elder brother's son Tanliang had escaped and was already safe; hearing of Zhaoguang's death he sighed and said: "The family gate has been butchered to extinction — why go on living!"
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Tanliang had escaped and was already safe; when he heard of Zhaoguang's death he sighed, "Our house is slaughtered to the last — what reason is there to live?"

sentences.zh: 絕吭而死。

translations.literal: He cut his throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: He cut his own throat and died.

sentences.zh: 初，太尉陳顯達自以高、武舊將，當高宗之世，內懷危懼，深自貶損，常乘朽弊車，道從鹵簿止用羸小者十數人。

translations.literal: Earlier, Grand Commandant Chen Xianda, considering himself an old general of Emperor Gao and Emperor Wu, during Emperor Gaozong's reign harbored inner fear, deeply humbled himself, constantly rode a broken-down cart, and in his processional guard used only a dozen or so weak small attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Chen Xianda, a veteran of the Gao and Wu reigns, had lived in dread under Emperor Gaozong. He humbled himself deliberately — riding a broken cart and keeping only a dozen frail attendants in his guard.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍宴，酒酣，啟高宗借枕，高宗令與之。

translations.literal: Once while attending a banquet, when wine was deep he requested of Gaozong to borrow a pillow; Gaozong ordered it given to him.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a banquet, well into his cups, he asked Emperor Gaozong for a pillow; the emperor granted it.

sentences.zh: 顯達撫枕曰：「臣年衰老，富貴已足，唯欠枕枕死，特就陛下乞之。」

translations.literal: Xianda caressed the pillow and said: "Your subject's years are old and feeble; wealth and honor are already sufficient — only lacking a pillow to die upon; I especially come before Your Majesty to beg for it."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianda stroked the pillow and said, "I am old, my lord, and have had wealth and honor enough. All I lack is a pillow to die on — I come to beg that of Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 高宗失色曰：「公醉矣！」

translations.literal: Gaozong changed color and said: "You are drunk!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong blanched. "You are drunk, sir!"

sentences.zh: 顯達以年禮告退，高宗不許。

translations.literal: Xianda requested retirement on grounds of age and the rites; Gaozong did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianda later asked to retire on grounds of age; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 及王敬則反，時顯達將兵拒魏，始安王遙光疑之，啟高宗欲追軍還；

translations.literal: When Wang Jingze rebelled, at the time Xianda was leading troops to resist Wei; Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an suspected him and reported to Gaozong wishing to recall the army;
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jingze rebelled, Chen Xianda was on campaign against Wei. Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an grew suspicious and petitioned Emperor Gaozong to recall his army;

sentences.zh: 會敬則平，乃止。

translations.literal: it happened that Jingze was pacified, and so he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: but Jingze was suppressed before the order went out, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 及帝即位，顯達彌不樂在建康。

translations.literal: When the Emperor acceded, Xianda was all the more unhappy staying in Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: After Donghun acceded, Chen Xianda grew ever more reluctant to remain in the capital.

sentences.zh: 得江州。

translations.literal: He obtained Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was given Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 甚喜。

translations.literal: He was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He was delighted.

sentences.zh: 嘗有疾，不令治，既而自愈，意甚不悅。

translations.literal: Once he had an illness and would not allow treatment; afterward it healed on its own, and he was very displeased in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he fell ill he refused treatment; when he recovered on his own he was deeply displeased — he had wanted to die.

sentences.zh: 聞帝屢誅大臣，傳雲當遣兵襲江州，十一月，丙辰，顯達舉兵於尋陽，令長史庾弘遠等與朝貴書，數帝罪惡，云「欲奉建安王為主，須京塵一靜，西迎大駕。」

translations.literal: Hearing that the Emperor repeatedly executed great ministers and that rumor said troops would be sent to attack Jiang Province, in the eleventh month, on bingchen, Xianda raised troops at Xunyang, ordering Chief Administrator Yu Hongyuan and others to write to court dignitaries listing the Emperor's crimes, saying: "We wish to install Prince Jian'an as sovereign; once the dust of the capital is stilled, we shall welcome the imperial carriage from the west."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the emperor's serial killings of ministers and rumors that troops would strike Jiang Province, Chen Xianda rose at Xunyang in the eleventh month on bingchen. His chief administrator Yu Hongyuan wrote to court grandees enumerating the emperor's crimes: "We mean to install Prince Jian'an as ruler; once the capital is quiet, we shall escort the imperial carriage westward."

sentences.zh: 乙丑，以護軍將軍崔慧景為平南將軍，督眾軍擊顯達；

translations.literal: On yichou General Who Protects the Army Cui Huijing was made General Who Pacifies the South and directed the various armies to strike Xianda;
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Cui Huijing, General Who Protects the Army, was made General Who Pacifies the South and placed in command of all forces against Chen Xianda;

sentences.zh: 後軍將軍胡松、驍騎將軍李叔獻帥水軍據梁山；

translations.literal: Rear General Hu Song and General of Valiant Cavalry Li Shuxian led the water army to occupy Liangshan;
translations.idiomatic: Rear General Hu Song and General of Valiant Cavalry Li Shuxian took the navy to hold Liangshan;

sentences.zh: 左衛將軍左興盛督前鋒軍屯杜姥宅。

translations.literal: Left Guard General Zuo Xingsheng directed the vanguard army and encamped at Old Lady Du's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard General Zuo Xingsheng commanded the vanguard and encamped at Old Lady Du's mansion.

sentences.zh: 十二月，癸未，以前輔國將軍楊集始為秦州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on guiwei, former General Who Assists the State Yang Jishi was made governor of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on guiwei, former General Who Assists the State Yang Jishi was appointed governor of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 陳顯達發尋陽，敗胡松於採石，建康震恐。

translations.literal: Chen Xianda set out from Xunyang, defeated Hu Song at Caishi; Jiankang shook with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianda marched from Xunyang and routed Hu Song at Caishi; the capital was stricken with fear.

sentences.zh: 甲申，軍於新林，左興盛帥諸軍拒之。

translations.literal: On jiashen he encamped at Xinlin; Zuo Xingsheng led the various armies to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Chen Xianda camped at Xinlin; Zuo Xingsheng led the imperial armies to block him.

sentences.zh: 顯達多置屯火於岸側，潛軍夜渡，襲宮城。

translations.literal: Xianda placed many campfires along the riverbank as a screen, secretly crossed the river by night with his army, and attacked the palace city.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianda lit decoy fires along the bank, slipped troops across the river by night, and struck at the palace.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，顯達以數千人登落星岡，新亭諸軍聞之，奔還，宮城大駭，閉門設守。

translations.literal: On yiyou Xianda with several thousand men ascended Luoxing Hill; the armies at Xinting hearing this fled back; the palace city was greatly alarmed, closed its gates and set defenses.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou Chen Xianda scaled Luoxing Hill with several thousand men. Troops at Xinting broke and ran back; the palace shut its gates in panic and manned the defenses.

sentences.zh: 顯達執馬槊，從步兵數百，於西州前與台軍戰，再合，顯達大勝，手殺數人，槊折；

translations.literal: Xianda grasped a cavalry lance, followed by several hundred infantry, and at the front of Xizhou fought with the capital garrison; twice they joined battle; Xianda won a great victory, personally killing several men; his lance broke;
translations.idiomatic: Wielding a lance at the head of several hundred foot soldiers, Chen Xianda fought imperial troops before Xizhou twice and won both engagements, killing several men himself until his lance snapped;

sentences.zh: 台軍繼至，顯達不能抗，退走，至西州後，騎官趙潭注刺顯達，墜馬，斬之，諸子皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Capital garrison troops continued arriving; Xianda could not resist, retreated and fled; reaching the rear of Xizhou, cavalry officer Zhao Tan thrust and stabbed Xianda; he fell from his horse and was beheaded; all his sons were executed.
translations.idiomatic: More imperial troops kept arriving until Chen Xianda could hold no longer. As he fell back past Xizhou, cavalry officer Zhao Tan ran him through with a lance; Xianda fell from his horse and was beheaded, and all his sons were executed.

sentences.zh: 長史庾弘遠，炳之之子也，斬於朱雀航。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Yu Hongyuan, son of Bingzhi, was beheaded at Zhuque Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Hongyuan, the chief administrator and son of Yu Bingzhi, was executed at Zhuque Bridge.

sentences.zh: 將刑，索帽著之，曰：「子路結纓，吾不可以不冠而死。」

translations.literal: About to be executed, he asked for a cap and put it on, saying: "Zilu tied his capstrings — I cannot die uncapped."
translations.idiomatic: Facing execution, he asked for a cap and put it on. "Zilu adjusted his capstrings before death," he said; "I cannot die bareheaded."

sentences.zh: 謂觀者曰：「吾非賊，乃是義兵，為諸軍請命耳。

translations.literal: He said to those watching: "I am not a rebel but a righteous army, pleading on behalf of the various armies, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: He addressed the onlookers: "I am no rebel but a man of principle, pleading for the armies — that is all.

sentences.zh: 陳公太輕事；

translations.literal: Lord Chen took the affair too lightly;
translations.idiomatic: Master Chen took matters too lightly;

sentences.zh: 若用吾言，天下將免塗炭。」

translations.literal: if he had used my words, the realm would have been spared annihilation."
translations.idiomatic: had he heeded my counsel, the realm would have been spared such ruin."

sentences.zh: 弘遠子子曜，抱父乞代命，並殺之。

translations.literal: Hongyuan's son Ziyao, embracing his father, begged to die in his stead; both were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyuan's son Ziyao clung to his father and begged to die in his place; both were killed.

sentences.zh: 帝既誅顯達，益自驕恣，漸出遊走，又不欲人見之；

translations.literal: The Emperor, having executed Xianda, was all the more arrogant and unrestrained, gradually going out to roam, yet not wishing to be seen;
translations.idiomatic: After killing Chen Xianda, the emperor grew ever more arrogant and began venturing out more often — yet he did not want to be seen;

sentences.zh: 每出，先驅斥所過人家，唯置空宅。

translations.literal: Every time he went out, advance riders cleared the households along the route; only empty dwellings were left.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went abroad, advance riders emptied every house along his route, leaving only deserted buildings behind.

sentences.zh: 尉司擊鼓蹋圍，鼓聲所聞，便應奔走，不暇衣履，犯禁者應手格殺。

translations.literal: The commandery officers beat drums and patrolled the cordon; wherever the drum sound was heard people had to run at once, without time for clothes or shoes; those who violated the prohibition were killed on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery officers beat drums and swept the cordon; wherever drums sounded people had to run at once, often without time for clothes or shoes, and anyone who broke curfew was killed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 一月凡二十餘出，出輒不言定所，東西南北，無處不驅。

translations.literal: In a month he went out more than twenty times; when he went out he never announced a fixed destination, and east, west, south, and north—there was no place he did not drive through.
translations.idiomatic: In a month he went out more than twenty times, never announcing where he was bound, driving everywhere in every direction.

sentences.zh: 常以三四更中，鼓聲四出，火光照天，幡戟橫路。

translations.literal: He often went out between the third and fourth watches; drums sounded on all sides, firelight filled the sky, and banners and halberds blocked the roads.
translations.idiomatic: He often went out between the third and fourth watches, with drums on every side, firelight filling the sky, and banners and halberds blocking the roads.

sentences.zh: 士民喧走相隨，老小震驚，啼號塞道，處處禁斷，不知所過。

translations.literal: Gentry and commoners ran shouting in his train; old and young were shaken with terror, wailing filled the roads, barriers were set everywhere, and none knew where he would pass.
translations.idiomatic: Citizens ran shouting in his wake; old and young were terrified, wails filled the streets, barriers went up everywhere, and no one knew which way he would go.

sentences.zh: 四民廢業，樵蘇路斷，吉凶失時，乳婦寄產，或輿病棄屍，不得殯葬。

translations.literal: The four classes of people abandoned their trades; woodcutters and fuel-gatherers could not travel the roads; auspicious and inauspicious affairs missed their seasons; nursing mothers gave birth in lodging houses; some carried the sick or abandoned corpses and could not bury them.
translations.idiomatic: All four classes of people abandoned their trades; woodcutters and fuel-gatherers could not use the roads; weddings and funerals missed their seasons; nursing mothers gave birth in rented rooms; some carried the sick or abandoned corpses and could not bury them.

sentences.zh: 巷陌懸幔為高鄣，置伏人防守，謂之「屏除」，亦謂之「長圍」。

translations.literal: In lanes and alleys they hung curtains as high barriers and posted men in ambush to guard them, calling this "screening out" and also "the long cordon."
translations.idiomatic: In streets and alleys they hung curtains as high barriers and posted hidden guards, calling it "screening out" or "the long cordon."

sentences.zh: 嘗至沈公城，有一婦人臨產，不去，因剖腹視其男女。

translations.literal: Once when he reached Duke Shen's town there was a woman about to give birth who did not leave; he had her belly cut open to see whether the child was male or female.
translations.idiomatic: Once at Duke Shen's town a woman in labor would not leave the street; he had her belly cut open to see whether the child was male or female.

sentences.zh: 又嘗至定林寺，有沙門老病不能去，藏草間；

translations.literal: Again when he reached Dinglin Monastery there was a monk, old and ill, who could not leave and hid in the grass;
translations.idiomatic: At Dinglin Monastery an old, sick monk who could not flee hid in the grass;

sentences.zh: 命左右射之，百箭俱發。

translations.literal: he ordered his attendants to shoot him, and a hundred arrows were loosed together.
translations.idiomatic: he ordered his attendants to shoot him, and a hundred arrows flew at once.

sentences.zh: 帝有膂力，牽弓至三斛五斗。

translations.literal: The emperor had great strength and could draw a bow to three hu and five dou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was powerfully built and could draw a bow rated at three hu and five dou.

sentences.zh: 又好擔幢，白虎幢高七丈五尺，於齒上擔之，折齒不倦。

translations.literal: He also loved carrying ceremonial banners; the White Tiger banner was seven zhang and five chi high—he shouldered it on the toothed pole, breaking teeth without tiring.
translations.idiomatic: He also loved carrying ceremonial banners; the White Tiger banner stood seven zhang and five chi high—he bore it on the toothed pole, breaking teeth without tiring.

sentences.zh: 自製擔幢校具，伎衣飾以金玉，侍衛滿側，逞諸變態，曾無愧色。

translations.literal: He himself made the fittings for carrying banners; performers' garments were adorned with gold and jade; guards filled his sides; he displayed every sort of grotesque stunt and never showed a trace of shame.
translations.idiomatic: He designed his own banner gear; performers' costumes were studded with gold and jade; guards lined both sides as he performed every grotesque stunt without a trace of shame.

sentences.zh: 學乘馬於東冶營兵俞靈韻，常著織成褲褶，金薄帽，執七寶槊，急裝縛褲，凌冒雨雪，不避坑阱。

translations.literal: He learned horsemanship from Yu Lingyun, a soldier of the Eastern Forge camp; he often wore woven trousers and jacket, a gold-foil cap, and grasped a seven-jeweled lance; in rapid dress with leggings bound he charged through rain and snow and did not avoid pits and traps.
translations.idiomatic: He learned riding from Yu Lingyun, a soldier of the Eastern Forge camp, often wearing brocade trousers and jacket, a gold-foil cap, and a seven-jeweled lance; dressed for speed with leggings bound tight, he charged through rain and snow and ignored pits and traps.

sentences.zh: 馳騁渴乏，輒下馬，解取腰邊蠡器，酌水飲之，復上馬馳去。

translations.literal: When he grew thirsty from galloping he would dismount at once, take the gourd vessel at his waist, pour water and drink, then mount again and gallop away.
translations.idiomatic: When thirst overtook him on the gallop he would dismount, take the gourd at his belt, drink, and ride off again.

sentences.zh: 又選無賴小人善走者為逐馬左右五百人，常以自隨。

translations.literal: He also selected five hundred ruffians and petty men skilled at running to serve as horse-chasers at his side, and constantly kept them with him.
translations.idiomatic: He also chose five hundred ruffians who could run well to chase beside his horse, and kept them with him constantly.

sentences.zh: 或於市側過親幸家，環回宛轉，周遍城邑。

translations.literal: Sometimes he passed the homes of his favorites at the market edge, wheeling and turning until he had circled the whole city.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he would pass the homes of his favorites by the market, wheeling about until he had covered the whole city.

sentences.zh: 或出郊射雉，置射雉場二百九十六處，奔走往來，略不暇息。

translations.literal: Sometimes he went to the suburbs to shoot pheasants, establishing two hundred ninety-six pheasant-shooting grounds, running back and forth with scarcely a moment's rest.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he went to the suburbs to shoot pheasants, setting up two hundred ninety-six shooting grounds and racing between them with scarcely a moment's rest.

sentences.zh: 王肅為魏制官品百司，皆如江南之制，凡九品，品各有二。

translations.literal: Wang Su for Wei established ranks for the hundred offices, all like the system of the lands south of the Yangtze: nine ranks in all, each rank having two grades.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su devised Wei's official ranking for the hundred offices on the southern model: nine ranks in all, each with two grades.

sentences.zh: 侍中郭祚兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Guo Zuo was concurrent Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Guo Zuo also served as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 祚清謹，重惜官位，每有銓授，雖得其人，必徘徊久，然後下筆，曰：「此人便己貴矣。」

translations.literal: Zuo was pure and cautious and greatly cherished official posts; whenever there was an appointment, even when he had the right man he would hesitate a long while before putting brush to paper, saying: "This man will already be exalted."
translations.idiomatic: Zuo was scrupulous and treasured official posts; for every appointment, even when he had the right man, he would hesitate a long while before signing, saying, "This man will already be exalted."

sentences.zh: 人以是多怨之；

translations.literal: Because of this many resented him;
translations.idiomatic: Many resented him for this;

sentences.zh: 然所用者無不稱職。

translations.literal: yet those he employed were without exception fit for their duties.
translations.idiomatic: yet every man he appointed proved fit for his post.
